f: Who was Mawlānā Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Shaykh Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī was a major Naqshbandī shaykh, scholar, spiritual guide, and influential figure in the Caucasian jihād movement of the 19th century.

f: When and where was Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī born?
b: He was born in 1203 AH / 1787 CE in Ghāzī Ghūmūq, the capital of Ghumuq, in the Avar regions of southern Dagestan.

f: What was the lineage of Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: His father was of Ḥusaynī lineage and his mother was of Ḥasanī origin, so he combined noble Prophetic lineage through both sides of his family.

f: How was Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī described by the author of Hadāyā al-Zamān?
b: He was described as “the shaykh of shaykhs, the beauty of the spiritual realms, the pole of guidance, and the possessor of assistance and divine support.”

f: How did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī begin his pursuit of knowledge?
b: His father, who was a scholar, directed him toward seeking knowledge and memorizing the Qur’an. He completed Qur’an memorization in the early years of his youth.

f: From whom did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī receive his early scholarly education?
b: He studied under the scholars of his time and the well-known shaykhs of his homeland.

f: Which languages and sciences did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī study?
b: He studied Arabic, memorized Prophetic hadith, and learned other sciences, including some practical sciences.

f: What level of hadith knowledge did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī attain?
b: He reached a very high level in hadith, memorizing a vast number of narrations along with their chains of transmission and texts, including authentic, weak, and fabricated narrations.

f: Why was Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī considered a scholar of exceptional rank?
b: Because of his vast knowledge across many fields, he became regarded as an encyclopedic scholar of his region and attained a distinguished rank among his contemporaries.

f: What position did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī hold under Sultan Aslan Khan of the Avars?
b: He served as a secretary/editor (muḥarrir) for Sultan Aslan Khan in his city of Ghāzī Ghūmūq.

f: Why was the position of secretary considered a scholarly position at that time?
b: The position required knowledge of Islamic sciences, Arabic, Turkish, and the person's native language, meaning it was only given to highly educated individuals.

f: How did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī enter the Naqshbandī path?
b: He came to the camp of the mujāhidīn on the same day that his shaykh, Shaykh Muḥammad Afandī al-Yarāghī, arrived. He then pledged allegiance to him in the Naqshbandī path.

f: From whom did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī receive his Naqshbandī training?
b: He continued learning from the scholars among the mujāhidīn and from his shaykh, Muḥammad Afandī al-Yarāghī, who lived among the frontier fighters (thughūr).

f: What role did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī have in the leadership of the Caucasian resistance?
b: He was part of the close council that made military decisions and issued religious rulings, and people referred to him for matters both major and minor.

f: To whom did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī himself refer for guidance?
b: Despite his own position, he continued referring to his shaykh Muḥammad Afandī al-Yarāghī for guidance in all matters.

f: What was the nature of Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s influence on the Caucasian jihād movement?
b: His influence was immense; he did not influence the movement merely as a thinker, commander, or scholar, but as a spiritual shaykh guiding his disciples.

f: How did the murīds respond to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s guidance?
b: They responded with love, obedience, attachment, loyalty, learning, spiritual training, and purification of the soul (tazkiyah).

f: How did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī contribute to spreading Islam in the Caucasus?
b: He trained his disciples into preachers and sent them throughout the Caucasus, not only Dagestan, to spread religious knowledge and guidance.

f: How do historical sources describe Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s role in the Dagestani murīd movement?
b: Historical sources describe him as the imam of the revolution, its true leader, and the spiritual guide of its jihād movement.

f: What was Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s role in the Naqshbandī order?
b: He was the guide of the Naqshbandī order and its imam throughout the Caucasus.

f: Was Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī affiliated with any other Sufi order besides the Naqshbandiyyah?
b: Yes. He was also granted authorization in the Qādiriyyah order, becoming the imam of both paths and the shaykh of both communities.

f: Why did people gather around Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī in the 19th century?
b: People gathered around him to unite in resisting oppression, aggression, and tyranny in Dagestan and the surrounding Muslim lands.

f: How did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī transform the military training camps?
b: He transformed the camps into places resembling Sufi lodges (zāwiyahs), where remembrance of Allah, supplication, repentance, spiritual devotion, and acts of worship were practiced day and night.

f: What was the spiritual atmosphere of Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s camps?
b: The camps were not only places of military preparation but also centers of dhikr, duʿāʾ, tawbah, spiritual retreat, and continuous worship.

f: What happened after Shaykh Muḥammad Afandī al-Yarāghī passed away in 1248 AH / 1844 CE?
b: Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Afandī al-Ghumuqī took the position of spiritual guidance (irshād) by unanimous agreement and became the recognized spiritual authority of the Naqshbandī path.

f: How widely was Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī accepted as a spiritual guide after his shaykh’s death?
b: He received complete acceptance, even from those who had received authorization from his own shaykh, such as Shaykh Abū Aḥmad al-Thughūrī.

f: How many people from Dagestan came to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī for spiritual guidance?
b: Countless people from Dagestan came to his presence, to the extent that their number could not be counted or fully recorded.

f: What effect did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī have on those who studied under him?
b: Many men reached spiritual completion through him and became accomplished disciples and guides.

f: Who were some of the notable successors and authorized deputies (khulafāʾ and maʾdhūnūn) of Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Among them were Shaykh Muḥammad Dabīr al-Rūjī (d. 1296 AH), Shaykh Ḥājj Yūsuf Afandī al-Khunāwī al-Sambūrī (martyred 1276 AH), Shaykh al-Ḥājj ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Thughūrī (d. 1299 AH), Shaykh Muḥammad al-Hakhālī, Shaykh al-Ḥājj Khalīl Afandī al-Janīghī al-Sambūrī (d. 1291 AH), Shaykh ʿUmar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ Muḥammad al-Hanūkhī al-Tafsīrānī (d. 1282 AH), and Shaykh Māl Muḥammad al-Tafsīrānī (d. 1281 AH).

f: What happened to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī after Imām Shāmil surrendered at Gunib in 1859 CE?
b: Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī moved with his family and close companions to the city of Temir Khan Shura, which was the headquarters of the Russian garrison.

f: What restrictions did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī face after moving to Temir Khan Shura?
b: He was placed under house arrest and remained there for a long period with his two eldest sons, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿAbd al-Raḥīm.

f: What happened to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s family after his period of house arrest?
b: A military order was issued to transfer his sons along with Imām Shāmil to his place of exile, while Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn migrated to Istanbul in 1873 CE.

f: How long did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī remain in Istanbul?
b: He remained in Istanbul for two years.

f: How did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī feel while living in Istanbul?
b: He longed for his family and homeland and was saddened by the events taking place there.

f: When and where did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī pass away?
b: He passed away in 1875 CE and was buried in the Dagestani cemetery of Karacaahmet in the Üsküdar district on the Asian side of Istanbul.

f: What writings did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī leave behind?
b: He left writings in his local language, several books, and an encyclopedic work on the Naqshbandī path titled Adab al-Murīdiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah.

f: What is the relationship between Adab al-Murīdiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah and al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: Al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah is the abridged version of his larger work Adab al-Murīdiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah.

f: In what language were Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s works written?
b: Both works were written in Arabic.

f: Into which languages was al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah translated?
b: It was translated into several languages, including Russian, and was printed in Tbilisi, Georgia, in 1869 CE.

f: What spiritual qualities were attributed to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Many miracles (karāmāt), elevated spiritual states, and remarkable divine gifts were attributed to him.

f: What does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī begin his introduction with?
b: He begins with Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm and the statement: “There is no power nor strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.”

f: How does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī describe the virtue of remembering Allah (dhikr)?
b: He states that remembering Allah is among the noblest acts of obedience and greatest forms of worship, and that it is a means of reaching Allah’s most sacred presence and ascending to the highest spiritual ranks.

f: What special honor does Allah give to those who remember Him according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Allah makes the one who remembers Him His companion and distinguishes the person who remembers Him from the rest of creation.

f: How does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī describe the Prophet ﷺ in his introduction?
b: He describes the Prophet ﷺ as the secret of existence and the master of creation, and he sends blessings upon him, his family, and his Companions who struggled in his path and attained the highest ranks.

f: What does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī say about himself in the introduction?
b: He humbly refers to himself as “the sinful and offending servant, Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī,” asking Allah to envelop him in His mercy and admit him into His spacious Paradise.

f: What does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī consider the greatest and noblest state of action?
b: He considers following the Sunnah in every circumstance to be the greatest action and the noblest spiritual state.

f: Why is following the Sunnah connected to travelling a spiritual path (sulūk) according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Because true adherence to the Sunnah can only be achieved through travelling a path of servitude that was transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ through the Companions to the Sufi shaykhs.

f: Why does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī consider the Naqshbandī path among the highest and best spiritual paths?
b: He considers it superior because it preserved its original form without additions or reductions and remained upon the way practiced by the Companions.

f: What does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī claim distinguishes the Naqshbandī path from other Sufi practices?
b: He states that it is free from innovations that some Sufi shaykhs introduced, such as loud dhikr, musical audition (samāʿ), dancing, ecstatic states, and deliberate attempts to induce spiritual emotions.

f: Why did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī criticize certain Sufi practices?
b: He criticized additions and practices that he considered contrary to the Qur’an, Sunnah, and the practice of the Prophet ﷺ, the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and the Companions, not the principles of spiritual purification, dhikr, love of Allah, or spiritual states themselves.

f: What clarification does the author give regarding Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī’s preference for the Naqshbandī path?
b: The preference was not merely because he belonged to the Naqshbandī order, but because he believed it preserved the original Sharīʿah-based method and avoided innovations.

f: What principle does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī emphasize when judging spiritual practices?
b: He emphasizes judging by the actual content and meaning of practices rather than merely by names and labels.

f: Why did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī write al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: He wanted to explain the manners and etiquettes needed by spiritual seekers (sālikūn), gathering them briefly and conveniently from reliable books, so that the work would become a means for his brothers to pray for him and a cause for forgiveness.

f: What hope did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī express for his book?
b: He hoped that Allah would make it beneficial for humanity and a means leading to the Abode of Peace (Paradise), through the honor of the best of creation, the Prophet ﷺ.

f: How did Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī organize his book?
b: He organized it into eleven chapters (abwāb) and a conclusion (khātimah).

f: What is discussed in the first chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The first chapter discusses repentance (tawbah) and its virtues.

f: What is discussed in the second chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The second chapter discusses purifying the soul from blameworthy characteristics.

f: What is discussed in the third chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The third chapter discusses the manners and etiquettes of the exalted Naqshbandī path.

f: What is discussed in the fourth chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The fourth chapter discusses how to take the spiritual covenant (ʿahd) and receive instruction (talqīn).

f: What is discussed in the fifth chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The fifth chapter discusses the virtue of dhikr over other acts of worship.

f: What is discussed in the sixth chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The sixth chapter discusses the spiritual connection (rābiṭah) and how to engage in it.

f: What is discussed in the seventh chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The seventh chapter discusses engaging in the supreme dhikr using the Divine Name (ism al-dhāt) and the formula of negation and affirmation (nafy wa ithbāt).

f: What is discussed in the eighth chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The eighth chapter discusses spiritual watchfulness (murāqabah) and how to practice it.

f: What is discussed in the ninth chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The ninth chapter discusses verbal dhikr and other regular devotions, including prayer, Qur’an recitation, khatm, and similar practices.

f: What is discussed in the tenth chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The tenth chapter discusses the truthfulness and qualities of complete shaykhs, as well as loving and respecting them.

f: What is discussed in the eleventh chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The eleventh chapter discusses the foundational principles of the Naqshbandī path that every murīd must observe.

f: What is discussed in the conclusion of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: The conclusion mentions the shaykhs of the noble spiritual chain (silsilah) and their lineages, seeking blessings through mentioning their names.

f: What is the first obligation upon a murīd according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: The first obligation upon a murīd is to correct his creed by knowing what is necessary for Allah, what is permissible regarding Allah, and what is impossible regarding Allah.

f: Why does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī begin the spiritual path with correct belief?
b: Because spiritual purification and progress must be built upon sound Islamic belief and correct knowledge of Allah’s attributes.

f: What must a murīd learn regarding the prophets according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: A murīd must learn what is necessary, permissible, and impossible regarding the prophets عَلَيْهِمْ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ.

f: What must a murīd learn from the Qur’an at the beginning of the spiritual path?
b: A murīd must learn from the Qur’an whatever is indispensable and needed in every circumstance, limiting himself to the sufficient amount required.

f: Why should a murīd initially learn only the necessary amount of Qur’anic knowledge?
b: Because the purpose at this stage is to acquire what is essential for religious practice rather than becoming occupied with unnecessary details before spiritual purification.

f: What areas of Islamic law (fiqh) must a murīd learn according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: He must learn the rulings needed for purification and worship, including the manners and rulings of wuḍūʾ, ghusl, tayammum, removal of impurities, pillars of prayer, fasting, and other necessary matters from the acts of worship.

f: What should a murīd avoid studying before purifying his soul and cleansing his heart?
b: He should avoid engaging in other sciences beyond the necessary religious knowledge until he has purified his soul and cleansed his heart.

f: Why should a murīd prioritize purification of the soul before pursuing extensive knowledge?
b: Because before purification he remains trapped by his lower nature and needs to free his soul and polish the mirror of his heart from veils that prevent entering Allah’s presence, perceiving realities, and understanding subtle aspects of knowledge.

f: What prevents a person from entering the divine presence and understanding deeper realities according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Spiritual veils on the heart, caused by impurities of the soul and blameworthy traits, prevent a person from reaching divine proximity and understanding deeper truths.

f: Which spiritual diseases must a murīd remove from his heart?
b: He must purify his heart from traits such as arrogance, anger, envy, greed, and other blameworthy qualities.

f: What should a murīd do after purifying his heart from blameworthy traits?
b: He should renew his repentance according to its conditions and then devote himself to worshipping Allah and performing dhikr according to the guidance of his shaykh.

f: What are the necessary attributes of Allah that a person must know according to the Naqshbandī creed presented here?
b: They are the twenty necessary attributes of Allah, including existence, pre-eternity, everlastingness, difference from creation, self-subsistence, oneness, and the seven attributes of meaning: power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, seeing, and speech, along with their corresponding relational attributes.

f: What are the permissible matters regarding Allah according to Islamic theology?
b: The permissible matter regarding Allah is that He may do every possible thing or leave it undone.

f: How many impossible attributes regarding Allah are mentioned in this passage?
b: Twenty impossible attributes are mentioned, which are the opposites of the twenty necessary attributes.

f: Why are Muslims only required to know these specific attributes of Allah rather than all possible attributes?
b: Because Allah’s necessary and impossible attributes are numerous, but out of mercy for human weakness, people are only required to know these twenty necessary attributes and their opposites.

f: What attributes are necessary for the prophets عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ?
b: The prophets must possess truthfulness (ṣidq), trustworthiness (amānah), conveying the revelation (tablīgh), infallibility (ʿiṣmah), and being male (dhukūrah).

f: What is impossible regarding the prophets عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ?
b: The opposites of their necessary attributes are impossible regarding them, such as lying, betrayal, concealing revelation, and moral corruption that contradicts their prophetic rank.

f: What human characteristics are permissible for prophets عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ?
b: Human characteristics that do not diminish their elevated rank are permissible for them, such as illness, marriage, eating, drinking, and other normal human conditions.

f: What is the proper order of the murīd’s spiritual development according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: The murīd should first correct his creed, learn essential Qur’an and fiqh, purify his soul and heart, remove blameworthy traits, renew repentance, and then engage in worship and dhikr according to the instruction of his shaykh.

f: What is the first chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah about?
b: The first chapter explains repentance (tawbah) and its virtues.

f: What is the linguistic meaning of tawbah (repentance)?
b: Linguistically, tawbah means returning. It is said: “tāba” when someone returns.

f: What is the religious definition of tawbah according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Tawbah is returning to Allah from what is blameworthy in the Sharīʿah to what is praiseworthy in it.

f: What are the conditions of sincere repentance?
b: The conditions are: feeling regret for past sins, immediately abandoning the sin, and resolving not to return to it in the future.

f: What additional condition applies when a sin involves the rights of another person?
b: If the sin involves another person’s rights, the wrongdoer must return the rights or property taken and seek the forgiveness and satisfaction of those wronged.

f: Is repentance obligatory immediately or can it be delayed?
b: Repentance is immediately obligatory by consensus, because abandoning sins is continuously obligatory.

f: Why is repentance considered the first step of the spiritual path?
b: Repentance is the gateway through which the servant enters the presence of the Lord of the worlds and is the first station where the spiritual traveller begins his ascent to higher stations.

f: What benefits does repentance bring to the servant?
b: Repentance saves the servant from destruction and frees him from the Fire in the eternal abode.

f: What Qur’anic verses does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī mention regarding the virtue of repentance?
b: He mentions: “O you who believe, repent to Allah with sincere repentance” (Qur’an 66:8); “And repent to Allah all together, O believers, so that you may be successful” (Qur’an 24:31); and “Indeed Allah loves those who constantly repent and those who purify themselves” (Qur’an 2:222).

f: What does the Qur’anic phrase “tawbatan naṣūḥā” (sincere repentance) mean according to this discussion?
b: It refers to sincere repentance that involves returning to Allah with regret, abandoning sin, and resolving not to return to it.

f: What hadith indicates that a person who repents becomes like someone without sin?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The one who repents from a sin is like one who has no sin.”

f: What hadith is mentioned about Allah’s love for those who repent?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The one who repents is beloved by Allah.”

f: Until when does Allah accept a person’s repentance according to the hadith?
b: Allah accepts the servant’s repentance as long as the soul has not reached the throat (before the final stages of death).

f: How does the Prophet ﷺ describe Allah’s joy at a servant’s repentance?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a person who loses his riding animal with his food and drink in a barren land, then unexpectedly finds it again.

f: What lesson is contained in the hadith about Allah’s joy at repentance?
b: It demonstrates the immense mercy of Allah and His great happiness when His servants return to Him, even though He is not in need of their repentance.

f: What happens to a person’s recorded sins after sincere repentance according to the mentioned narration?
b: Allah causes the recording angels to forget the sins they recorded, causes the person’s limbs to forget the sins committed, and removes the evidence of those sins, so that the person meets Allah without witnesses against him from creation.

f: What transformation of past sins is mentioned regarding those who sincerely repent?
b: Some scholars mention that when a servant sincerely repents, Allah can transform his previous sins into good deeds.

f: Which Qur’anic verse indicates that sins can be transformed into good deeds?
b: The verse: “Except those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds” (Qur’an 25:70).

f: Why does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī mention stories of repentant people?
b: He mentions them to show the vastness of Allah’s mercy and His favor toward sinful servants who return to Him.

f: How many stories of repentant people does Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī intend to mention?
b: He intends to mention five stories of repentant people as examples of Allah’s mercy and forgiveness.

f: How did classical scholars define tawbah similarly to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Scholars such as al-Ghazālī and Ibn al-Qayyim defined tawbah as regret over past sins, abandoning them immediately, resolving not to return to them, and correcting previous shortcomings.

f: What is the first repentance story mentioned by Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: It is the story of Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī, who witnessed an event involving a scorpion, a frog, a snake, and a sleeping drunk man, which became a means of repentance for the man.

f: Who was Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī?
b: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī was a famous Egyptian ascetic and spiritual master. His name was Thawbān ibn Ibrāhīm (also reported as Fayḍ ibn Ibrāhīm), known by the kunyah Abū al-Fayḍ or Abū al-Fayyāḍ. He lived from approximately 179–245 AH and was regarded as the ascetic shaykh of Egypt.

f: What did Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī see while walking along the Nile?
b: He saw a scorpion crawling and picked up a stone intending to kill it, but the scorpion quickly fled and stopped at the bank of the Nile.

f: How did the scorpion cross the Nile?
b: A frog emerged from the water, the scorpion climbed onto its back, and the frog carried it across the Nile to the other side.

f: What did Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī do after seeing the scorpion cross the Nile?
b: He followed the scorpion to the other side of the Nile to see what would happen.

f: What did the scorpion do after reaching the other side of the Nile?
b: The scorpion climbed off the frog’s back and approached a sleeping man who was intoxicated.

f: What danger did the sleeping man face?
b: A snake approached the sleeping man intending to bite and kill him.

f: How did the scorpion save the sleeping man?
b: The scorpion rushed toward the snake and stung it so severely that the snake was torn into pieces, saving the man from being bitten.

f: What did Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī do after the scorpion killed the snake?
b: He woke the sleeping man and told him that the danger had been removed.

f: How did the man react when he saw the dead snake?
b: He became frightened and ran away, but Dhū al-Nūn told him not to fear because the matter had already been taken care of.

f: How did the man respond after hearing the story of how Allah saved him?
b: He lowered his head in reflection, looked toward the sky, and said: “O my Lord, this is how You treat the one who disobeys You; then how will You treat the one who obeys You? By Your might and majesty, I will never disobey You again.”

f: What did the man do after resolving to repent?
b: He left while crying, reciting verses expressing amazement that people sleep while Allah protects them from dangers in the darkness and grants them blessings.

f: What spiritual lesson does the story of Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī and the drunk man illustrate?
b: The story illustrates Allah’s immense mercy toward His servants, His protection even of those who disobey Him, and how recognizing divine mercy can awaken sincere repentance.

f: What is the second repentance story mentioned by Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: It is the story of a Kurdish highway robber who repented after witnessing Allah’s mercy and care for His creatures.

f: What was the sinful occupation of the man in the second repentance story?
b: He used to rob travelers, cut off roads, and seize people’s wealth.

f: What happened while the Kurdish robber and his companions were preparing to rob people?
b: While sitting together after going out for robbery, he saw a remarkable event involving three palm trees.

f: What unusual thing did the Kurdish robber observe with the palm trees?
b: He saw a bird carrying a fresh date from a fruit-bearing palm tree to the top of a palm tree that had no dates, repeating this action ten times while he watched.

f: Why did the Kurdish robber climb the palm tree?
b: He became curious about what was happening and climbed the tree to investigate.

f: What did the Kurdish robber find at the top of the palm tree?
b: He found a blind snake with its mouth open, and the bird was placing fresh dates into its mouth.

f: How did the Kurdish robber react after seeing the bird feeding the blind snake?
b: He cried and reflected on Allah’s mercy, saying that although the snake was an animal that the Prophet ﷺ commanded to be killed, Allah had provided it with a bird to care for it.

f: What realization did the Kurdish robber have about his own situation?
b: He realized that while Allah cared for a blind snake, he himself was a servant who acknowledged Allah’s oneness but had been using his abilities to rob people and frighten travelers.

f: What spiritual message did the Kurdish robber receive after his reflection?
b: A voice came to his heart saying: “O so-and-so, My door is open,” meaning Allah’s door of repentance was open for him.

f: How did the Kurdish robber demonstrate his repentance?
b: He broke his sword, placed dust on his head, and called out asking Allah to forgive him and accept his repentance.

f: What response did the Kurdish robber receive after asking for forgiveness?
b: He heard a voice saying: “We have accepted you.”

f: How did the Kurdish robber’s companions react when they saw his transformation?
b: They asked him why he had disturbed them, and he told them that he had been abandoned but had now been reconciled with Allah.

f: What did the Kurdish robber’s companions do after hearing his story?
b: They also decided to repent, abandoned their clothing and weapons, entered into the state of iḥrām, and set out toward Makkah.

f: How long did the group walk through the wilderness on their way to Makkah?
b: They walked through the wilderness for three days.

f: What happened when the repentant group entered a village on their journey?
b: They encountered an elderly blind woman who asked whether one of them was the Kurdish man.

f: Why did the blind woman have clothing prepared for the Kurdish robber?
b: She said that her son had died and left behind those clothes, and she had seen the Prophet ﷺ in a dream for three nights telling her to give them to the Kurdish man.

f: What did the Kurdish robber and his companions do after receiving the clothing?
b: They wore the clothing and continued their journey to Makkah, where their lives changed completely.

f: What spiritual lesson does the story of the Kurdish robber illustrate?
b: It illustrates the vastness of Allah’s mercy, that His guidance can reach even the greatest sinners, and that observing Allah’s mercy toward creation can awaken sincere repentance.

f: What is the third repentance story mentioned by Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī, and what lesson does it teach?
b: It is the story of Shaykh ʿAlī ibn al-Murtaḍā and a sinful drummer who repented and reached a high spiritual rank. It teaches that Allah can transform a person completely through repentance and that spiritual stations are gifts from Allah, not merely the result of length of worship or companionship with a shaykh.

f: What happened when Shaykh ʿAlī ibn al-Murtaḍā was travelling from Zabīd toward the coast with his disciple?
b: On the way, he passed by a branch and told his disciple to take it. The disciple wondered about the reason but remained silent. They then reached a settlement of people who neglected worship, drank alcohol, ate carrion, and were engaged in singing, playing, and beating drums.

f: How did Shaykh ʿAlī ibn al-Murtaḍā guide the sinful drummer to repentance?
b: He called the tall drummer, had his disciple bring him, instructed the disciple to discipline him with the branch, then took him to the sea, taught him purification (ghusl and wuḍūʾ), taught him prayer, and prayed with him.

f: What extraordinary event occurred after the drummer repented and learned purification and prayer?
b: After the prayer, Shaykh ʿAlī ibn al-Murtaḍā placed his prayer mat on the sea and told the man to step onto it. The man walked upon the water until he disappeared from sight.

f: How did Shaykh ʿAlī ibn al-Murtaḍā’s disciple react to seeing the man receive such a spiritual rank so quickly?
b: The disciple was amazed and said that although he had accompanied the shaykh for many years, he had not attained such a station, while this man received such a rank in one hour.

f: What did Shaykh ʿAlī ibn al-Murtaḍā say about the man’s miracle and spiritual station?
b: He cried and said: “My son, what did you think? This is the action of Allah.” He explained that he had been commanded that one of the Abdāl had died and that this man should take his place, so he obeyed Allah’s command.

f: What is the main spiritual lesson from the story of Shaykh ʿAlī ibn al-Murtaḍā and the repentant man?
b: A person’s past sins do not prevent Allah from elevating him, and divine closeness and spiritual ranks are granted by Allah’s grace and will.

f: What is the fourth repentance story in al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah?
b: It is the story of Imām Abū al-Qāsim al-Junayd al-Baghdādī and a young singer who was granted a high spiritual rank.

f: Who was Imām Abū al-Qāsim al-Junayd al-Baghdādī?
b: He was the famous master of the Sufi path (Sayyid al-Ṭāʾifah) and one of the greatest spiritual teachers of Baghdad.

f: What did a righteous man who visited Imām al-Junayd tell him before his death?
b: He told al-Junayd that his meeting with Allah was near and instructed him to give his patched cloak, staff, and water container to a young singer who would come after his death.

f: Why was Imām al-Junayd surprised when he was told to give spiritual items to a singer?
b: He wondered how a singer could be worthy of receiving the belongings of a righteous spiritual man.

f: What did the righteous man say about the singer’s spiritual rank?
b: He said that the singer had reached that rank through his service to Allah.

f: Who came to Imām al-Junayd after the righteous man’s death?
b: A young Egyptian man came and asked for the entrusted cloak, staff, and water container.

f: How did the young Egyptian man know that he should receive Imām al-Junayd’s entrusted items?
b: He said that he heard a spiritual call telling him to go to al-Junayd and take the items because he had been appointed in place of a deceased Abdāl.

f: What did Imām al-Junayd do after hearing the young man’s explanation?
b: He gave him the cloak, staff, and water container.

f: What did the young Egyptian man do after receiving the belongings of the righteous man?
b: He performed ghusl, wore the patched cloak, and left travelling toward Syria.

f: What lesson does the story of Imām al-Junayd and the singer teach?
b: Allah can guide and elevate people whom others may overlook, and spiritual rank is a gift from Allah rather than being judged only by a person’s outward appearance or past.

f: What is the fifth repentance story mentioned by Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: It is the story of a sinful man whose sincere repentance caused Allah to forgive him and make him among His awliyāʾ.

f: What did Allah command Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ to do regarding one of His awliyāʾ?
b: Allah commanded Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ to go and pray over one of His awliyāʾ who had died in a certain place.

f: What did the people say about the deceased man when Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ asked about him?
b: They said he was a wicked sinner who persisted in major sins, and they were relieved that he had died.

f: What did Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ discover when he found the deceased man?
b: He found him thrown away in a rubbish area, covered with dust and ashes.

f: Why did Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ question Allah about the man’s status?
b: Because the people testified that the man had died while persisting in major sins, while Allah had called him one of His awliyāʾ.

f: Why did Allah forgive the sinful man and make him one of His awliyāʾ?
b: Near death, the man became thirsty, was refused water by people, and turned sincerely to Allah, asking forgiveness by the honor of Jibrīl, Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, and the revealed Book.

f: What realization did the sinful man have before his repentance?
b: He realized that although he had sinned against Allah, Allah had never deprived him of His provision, while people had refused him even a drink of water.

f: What was the result of the man’s sincere repentance?
b: Allah forgave him, had mercy on him, and made him among His awliyāʾ.

f: What are the three categories of matters related to repentance mentioned after the story?
b: The prerequisites (muqaddimāt), signs (ʿalāmāt), and fruits (thamarāt) of repentance.

f: What are the prerequisites of repentance?
b: Awakening the heart from heedlessness, recognizing one’s sinful state, fearing Allah’s punishment, and realizing one’s inability to endure the consequences of sin.

f: What are the signs of sincere repentance?
b: Leaving bad companions, avoiding unnecessary speech, increasing good deeds, maintaining dhikr, humility, sadness over past sins, crying, and constantly seeking Allah’s forgiveness.

f: What are the fruits of sincere repentance?
b: Returning to being beloved by Allah, having sins changed into good deeds, tasting the sweetness of worship and supplication, having deeds accepted, and regaining the light of faith in the heart.

f: How does repentance change a person’s relationship with Allah?
b: A person who was once close to Satan through sin becomes beloved to Allah through sincere repentance.

f: What happens to a repentant person’s spiritual state according to the passage?
b: The light of faith returns to the heart, and the angels perceive the fragrance of obedience instead of the foulness of sin.

f: What does this story teach about Allah’s mercy?
b: Allah’s mercy is immense; He can forgive many years of sins in a single moment through sincere repentance.

f: What are the two types of sins that require repentance?
b: Sins related to Allah’s rights and sins related to the rights of people.

f: How is repentance from Allah’s rights fulfilled?
b: It is fulfilled through regret and abandoning the sin, although some sins also require making up missed duties or performing expiation.

f: What additional requirements may apply to some sins against Allah’s rights?
b: Some require making up acts of worship, such as missed prayers or fasting, while others require expiation, such as breaking an oath.

f: How are sins involving the rights of other people repented from?
b: The rights must be returned to their rightful owners or the person wronged must be satisfied.

f: What should a person do if they cannot return the rights of others due to inability?
b: They should sincerely repent, and hope for Allah’s forgiveness and generosity.

f: What should a repentant person do after repentance?
b: They should increase good deeds, seek forgiveness for those they have wronged, and never despair of Allah’s mercy.

f: What should a person do if Allah grants them firmness in repentance?
b: They should praise and thank Allah, because steadfastness in obedience is a sign of divine success.

f: What should a person do if they fall back into sin after repenting?
b: They should repent again and continue returning to Allah without despairing of acceptance.

f: When does the door of repentance remain open?
b: The door of repentance remains open until the sun rises from the west.

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise Ḥabīb ibn al-Ḥārith when he said he repeatedly sinned and repented?
b: The Prophet ﷺ told him: “Whenever you sin, repent.” When he worried that his sins would increase, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah’s forgiveness is greater than your sins.”

f: What does the story of the man from the time of Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ teach about repentance?
b: It teaches that Allah’s mercy and forgiveness are greater than a servant’s sins when he sincerely turns back to Him.

f: What did Allah say to the man who repeatedly failed to remain upon repentance?
b: Allah first warned him of His anger, but after Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ pleaded for him, Allah forgave him because of his sincere supplication and hope in divine mercy.

f: What did Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ say when he heard Allah would not forgive the man?
b: He questioned how Allah’s mercy could be exhausted, since mercy is among Allah’s eternal attributes while sin is a temporary quality of creation.

f: How did Allah respond to Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ’s plea for the sinful man?
b: Allah told Mūsā to inform him that even if his sins filled the heavens and earth, He had forgiven him because of his sincere supplication.

f: What message did a repentant disciple receive when he wondered whether Allah would accept him again?
b: He heard: “You obeyed Us, so We thanked you; then you left Us, so We gave you time; if you return to Us, We will accept you.”

f: Why is repentance more necessary for a person than food, drink, and shelter?
b: Because sins create barriers between the servant and Allah, preventing closeness to Him and the realization of spiritual truths.

f: Why is repentance essential in the spiritual path (sulūk)?
b: Because the goal of the spiritual path is reaching Allah, and this cannot be achieved without removing the barriers of sin through sincere repentance.

f: What is the main lesson of this section on repentance?
b: A servant should never despair of Allah’s mercy; even after repeated failures, sincere repentance and returning to Allah remain possible.

f: What is the second chapter of al-Ādāb al-Marḍiyyah fī al-Ṭarīqah al-Naqshbandiyyah about?
b: It explains purification of the soul from blameworthy traits and adorning it with praiseworthy qualities.

f: What is the meaning of tazkiyah (purification of the soul)?
b: Tazkiyah means reforming and purifying the soul and heart, removing their impurities, and directing them toward Allah.

f: Why must a person purify the soul according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Because a person cannot draw near to the divine presence or witness the divine secrets without removing corrupt traits and developing noble qualities.

f: What is the relationship between spiritual purification and witnessing divine realities?
b: Purifying the soul removes the veils that prevent a person from approaching Allah and understanding deeper spiritual realities.

f: What does the saying “Adorn yourselves with the qualities of Allah” mean?
b: It means acquiring praiseworthy qualities and avoiding blameworthy ones, not taking on any divine attributes that belong only to Allah.

f: What is meant by “takhallī” and “taḥallī” in spiritual purification?
b: Takhallī means emptying the soul of blameworthy traits, while taḥallī means adorning it with virtues and acts of obedience.

f: What does tazkiyah require a person to remove from the soul?
b: It requires removing animalistic and base qualities such as envy, showing off, arrogance, self-admiration, and excessive love of the world.

f: What does tazkiyah require a person to develop in the soul?
b: It requires developing noble qualities such as chastity, courage, wisdom, and other virtues.

f: Why can a person not fully purify himself without following a spiritual path according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: Because the path of the Sufis is a path of refining character, learning the diseases of the soul, their cures, and the ways to acquire virtuous qualities.

f: What are the two main tasks involved in spiritual purification?
b: Knowing the blameworthy qualities and how to remove them, and knowing the praiseworthy qualities and how to acquire them.

f: What Qur’anic evidence is mentioned for the importance of soul purification?
b: Allah says: “Successful indeed is the one who purifies it, and failed is the one who corrupts it” (Qur’an 91:9–10).

f: What was one of the main missions of the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in relation to purification?
b: Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ to recite His verses, purify people, and teach them the Book and wisdom (Qur’an 62:2).

f: What reward is mentioned for those who purify themselves?
b: Those who purify themselves and perform righteous deeds receive the highest ranks and eternal gardens (Qur’an 20:75–76).

f: Is the phrase “Adorn yourselves with the qualities of Allah” authentically established as a Prophetic hadith?
b: It is commonly quoted, but no connected authentic chain of narration was found; some scholars considered it a statement of righteous predecessors.

f: How did scholars explain the meaning of “Adorn yourselves with the qualities of Allah”?
b: They explained it as adopting praiseworthy qualities and avoiding blameworthy qualities, not resembling Allah in His divine attributes.

f: How did ʿĀʾishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا describe the character of the Prophet ﷺ?
b: She said: “His character was the Qur’an.”

f: What does the statement “The character of the Prophet ﷺ was the Qur’an” indicate according to spiritual scholars?
b: It indicates that the Prophet ﷺ embodied the noble qualities and guidance contained in the Qur’an.

f: What are some of the blameworthy qualities that a seeker must remove through spiritual purification?
b: They include hatred, envy, anger, self-admiration (ʿujb), and pride (kibr).

f: What is hatred (ḥiqd), and how is it treated?
b: Hatred is hidden, continuous anger in the heart. It is treated by realizing that it harms its owner by keeping him in suffering and by seeing good in the person hated.

f: What is envy (ḥasad), and how is it treated?
b: Envy is wanting to possess all goodness for oneself and wishing that blessings disappear from others. It is treated by realizing that it benefits neither the envier nor harms the one envied; instead, the envier remains troubled while the envied enjoys blessings.

f: What is anger (ghaḍab), and how is it treated?
b: Anger is intense agitation of the soul seeking revenge. It is treated by recognizing that anger causes corruption, leads to sin and misguidance, and ends in regret.

f: What is self-admiration (ʿujb), and how is it treated?
b: Self-admiration is believing oneself to possess special perfection and being amazed by one’s own deeds. It is treated by remembering one’s own weakness and shortcomings and recognizing that others may be better.

f: What is pride (kibr)?
b: Pride is considering oneself superior to others because of qualities or greatness one believes one possesses.

f: How is pride (kibr) treated and removed from the heart?
b: By viewing oneself with humility, viewing others with respect, remembering the condemnation of pride in the Qur’an and Sunnah, and recognizing that greatness belongs only to Allah.

f: What is miserliness (bukhl), and how is it treated?
b: Miserliness is withholding wealth out of fear of poverty. It is treated by realizing that spending wealth in good causes is among the greatest acts of worship and brings closeness to Allah and love from people.

f: What is greed (ṭamaʿ), and how is it treated?
b: Greed is expecting benefit from others without deserving it. It is treated by realizing that greed brings neither benefit nor protection from harm, causes humiliation and lack of dignity, and that whatever Allah has decreed will reach a person without excessive seeking.

f: What is excessive desire (ḥirṣ), and how is it treated?
b: Excessive desire is an uncontrolled craving for the pleasures of the stomach and sexual desire. It is treated by eating less, fasting more, avoiding luxurious foods, maintaining remembrance and spiritual awareness, keeping company with righteous people, and avoiding harmful companionship.

f: What is laziness (baṭālah), and how is it treated?
b: Laziness is abandoning the pursuit of the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. It is treated by realizing that lazy people are deprived and by keeping company with those who strive, worship, and seek spiritual progress.

f: What is cowardice (jubn), and how is it treated?
b: Cowardice is avoiding what one should have the courage to do. It is treated by knowing that it brings blame and humiliation, that lifespans are already decreed, and that courage is a noble quality.

f: What is excessive love of the world (ḥubb al-dunyā), and how is it treated?
b: It is excessive desire to gather worldly wealth. It is treated by realizing that love of the world does not increase one’s possessions; rather, Allah’s giving and generosity increase them, and excessive worldly attachment is a cause of many sins.

f: What are some praiseworthy qualities that replace blameworthy qualities?
b: Among them are chastity (ʿiffah), love and compassion (wudd), and humility (tawāḍuʿ).

f: What is chastity (ʿiffah)?
b: Chastity is restraining the soul from animalistic desires and keeping it away from excessive passions.

f: What is the effect of having chastity (ʿiffah)?
b: A person with chastity gains control over the self and closeness to Allah.

f: What is love and compassion (wudd)?
b: Wudd is mercy and compassion toward others without selfish desire.

f: What is humility (tawāḍuʿ)?
b: Humility is abandoning self-glorification and treating people with honor and respect.

f: What is the result of developing humility?
b: A person becomes a source of spiritual benefit and gains acceptance among people.

f: What is meant by al-bashr (cheerfulness) as a praiseworthy character trait?
b: Al-bashr is showing happiness, friendliness, and a cheerful expression when meeting others. Whoever develops this trait becomes blessed and happy.

f: What does al-bashr include according to the scholars?
b: Al-bashr includes having a bright face, smiling, showing happiness, welcoming others warmly, and being gentle in interaction. It is the opposite of gloominess and harshness.

f: What examples from the Prophet ﷺ demonstrate the virtue of cheerfulness and good character?
b: The Prophet ﷺ was described as always cheerful, easy in character, and gentle. He said: “Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity,” and “Let them be encompassed by your cheerful face and good character.”

f: What is tawāḍuʿ (humility)?
b: Tawāḍuʿ is abandoning self-exaltation over others and treating people with respect and honor.

f: What is the spiritual benefit of humility?
b: Whoever develops humility becomes a person of blessing and acceptance, and Allah raises the one who humbles himself for His sake.

f: What evidence shows the virtue of humility in Islam?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one boasts over another or transgresses against another,” and “Whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him.”

f: What is salāmat al-ṣudūr (purity of hearts)?
b: Salāmat al-ṣudūr is having good thoughts about creation and looking at people with contentment rather than hatred, envy, or resentment.

f: What is the result of having purity of heart?
b: Whoever has purity of heart becomes a person of spiritual purity, peace, and openness.

f: What Quranic teachings encourage purity of the heart?
b: Allah praises those whose hearts are free from rancor and hatred, and He describes the people of Paradise as having purified hearts.

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about having a sound heart?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said he preferred to meet people while having a sound heart, and he described the best people as those with a pure heart free from sin, oppression, hatred, and envy.

f: What is sakhaʾ (generosity)?
b: Sakhaʾ is giving wealth to those who deserve it without seeking compensation, praise, or worldly benefit.

f: What is the spiritual effect of generosity?
b: Whoever develops generosity gains sincerity in intention and rises to higher spiritual ranks.

f: How is true generosity different from simply giving money?
b: True generosity is a quality of the soul that causes a person to give naturally without seeking reward, recognition, or personal benefit.

f: What is al-shajāʿah (courage) as a praiseworthy character trait?
b: Al-shajāʿah is advancing toward difficult matters without leaving the limits of the Sharīʿah. Whoever develops it becomes a person of dignity, awe, and honor.

f: What is the Islamic meaning of true courage?
b: True courage is having strength of heart and readiness to face hardships for the sake of truth while remaining within the commands of Islam.

f: What is the virtue of courage in Islam?
b: Courage gives a person dignity and strength. The Prophet ﷺ said: “The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both.”

f: How did Imam al-Nawawī explain the “strength” mentioned in the hadith of the strong believer?
b: He explained that it refers to strength of determination and resolve in matters of the Hereafter, such as striving in worship, commanding good, forbidding evil, and patiently bearing difficulties for Allah’s sake.

f: What is al-ṣabr (patience)?
b: Al-ṣabr is enduring trials and hardships in order to gain Allah’s pleasure in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever develops patience receives Allah’s support and victory.

f: What does patience require according to the scholars?
b: Patience requires restraining the soul from despair, complaints, and disobedience, while remaining firm upon Allah’s commands and accepting His decree.

f: What Quranic evidence shows the importance of patience?
b: Allah says: “O believers, be patient, persevere, remain steadfast, and fear Allah so that you may succeed.” Patience is mentioned many times throughout the Qur’an.

f: What is al-himmah (spiritual aspiration)?
b: Al-himmah is seeking Allah alone and turning away from everything besides Him. Whoever develops it becomes among those who reach Allah and are brought close to Him.

f: What is high spiritual aspiration (ʿulū al-himmah)?
b: It is directing the heart and all spiritual abilities toward Allah in order to attain perfection for oneself or others.

f: How did the scholars describe a person of high aspiration?
b: A person of high aspiration does not settle for low goals or worldly concerns but seeks the highest ranks of knowledge, action, and spiritual perfection.

f: What is the difference between high aspiration and worldly ambition?
b: High aspiration seeks Allah, perfection, and noble purposes, while worldly ambition is limited to desires such as wealth, status, and physical pleasures.

f: What did Ibn al-Jawzī say about high aspiration?
b: He explained that a person with true aspiration should always seek the highest level of perfection possible and not be content with a lower rank when a higher one can be attained.

f: What is al-wafāʾ (faithfulness) as a praiseworthy character trait?
b: Al-wafāʾ is fulfilling what one has committed to with the tongue while having a heart that is content and sincere. Whoever develops it becomes among those who receive blessings and good fortune.

f: What is the linguistic and technical meaning of al-wafāʾ?
b: Linguistically, al-wafāʾ is the opposite of betrayal and means completing and preserving a covenant. Technically, it means remaining upon loyalty, fulfilling promises, and maintaining the agreements made with others.

f: What Quranic teachings emphasize the importance of fulfilling promises?
b: Allah commands believers to fulfill His covenant, keep their agreements, fulfill their pledges, and not break oaths after confirming them.

f: What is kitmān al-sirr (keeping secrets)?
b: Kitmān al-sirr is preserving what one has been entrusted with regarding private matters and not revealing confidential information.

f: What is the spiritual effect of keeping secrets?
b: Whoever develops the quality of keeping secrets becomes a person of wisdom and knowledge and is brought close to Allah’s generosity and favor.

f: What Islamic evidence emphasizes the importance of keeping secrets and trusts?
b: Allah says: “Do not betray Allah and the Messenger ﷺ, nor betray your trusts while you know.” It is also reported that when two people sit together in trust, neither should reveal what the other dislikes being disclosed.

f: What did Imam al-Shāfiʿī say about keeping secrets?
b: He said that a person who reveals his own secret and then blames others is foolish, while the chest of the person entrusted with a secret is even narrower in keeping it.

f: What did Imam al-Ghazālī say about keeping secrets?
b: Imam al-Ghazālī said that the lowest level of nobility is keeping secrets, while the highest level is forgetting what was entrusted to you. He also said: “The chests of free people are the graves of secrets.”

f: What is al-qanāʿah (contentment) as a praiseworthy character trait?
b: Al-qanāʿah is the soul being satisfied with what Allah has provided without longing for increase. Whoever develops it becomes among those with honor and a lofty spiritual state.

f: What is the linguistic and technical meaning of al-qanāʿah?
b: Linguistically, al-qanāʿah means being satisfied and pleased. Technically, it means being content with what Allah has given, being satisfied with what is available, and not constantly seeking what is missing.

f: What did the scholars say about the meaning of al-qanāʿah?
b: They described it as being pleased with Allah’s provision, remaining calm when lacking worldly things, being satisfied with necessities, and not desiring beyond what Allah has granted.

f: What Quranic teachings encourage contentment and detachment from worldly life?
b: Allah reminds people that worldly life is temporary entertainment and that the Hereafter is the true life. He also teaches that lasting righteous deeds are better than worldly possessions.

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about zuhd (detachment from the world)?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Be detached from the world and Allah will love you, and be detached from what people possess and people will love you.”

f: What is al-zuhd (asceticism/detachment from the world)?
b: Al-zuhd is leaving worldly excess beyond what is necessary in order to devote oneself to obedience to Allah. Whoever develops it becomes beloved by Allah and accepted among people.

f: How did the early scholars define zuhd?
b: They defined zuhd as reducing attachment to the world, shortening one’s hopes, trusting Allah, not rejoicing excessively over worldly gains, and not grieving over worldly losses.

f: What is the relationship between zuhd and worldly possessions?
b: Zuhd does not necessarily mean abandoning all possessions; rather, it means that worldly things do not occupy the heart or distract a person from Allah.

f: What is al-tawakkul (reliance upon Allah)?
b: Al-tawakkul is not being overly concerned with acquiring what one needs while relying upon Allah’s generosity and provision.

f: What is the spiritual result of tawakkul?
b: Whoever develops true reliance upon Allah becomes a person of maʿrifah (spiritual knowledge and recognition of Allah).

f: What is the result of abandoning blameworthy qualities and adopting all praiseworthy qualities?
b: A person who removes bad traits and develops these virtues becomes a true follower of the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, among the righteous saints and chosen servants of Allah, reaching spiritual stations and being able to guide others to the truth.

f: What rank does a person attain after perfecting these spiritual qualities?
b: Such a person becomes among those who have reached Allah, traversed spiritual stations, guide people to the Sharīʿah and reality, and become a rightly guided representative in religion.

f: What is al-tawakkul (reliance upon Allah) linguistically and technically?
b: Linguistically, al-tawakkul means dependence and entrusting matters to another. Technically, it is the heart’s sincere reliance upon Allah for bringing benefits and removing harm in both worldly and religious matters.

f: What does relying upon Allah mean in practice?
b: It means depending on Allah alone, entrusting one’s affairs to Him, and not relying upon what people possess.

f: What is the ruling and importance of tawakkul in Islam?
b: Tawakkul is an obligation that must be sincerely directed to Allah. It is one of the greatest forms of worship and among the highest stations of tawḥīd because many righteous deeds arise from it.

f: What Quranic verses show the importance of tawakkul?
b: Allah says: “And upon Allah rely if you are believers” and “If you have believed in Allah, then upon Him rely if you are Muslims,” showing that tawakkul is connected to true faith and Islam.

f: How did al-Jurjānī define tawakkul?
b: Al-Jurjānī defined tawakkul as trusting in what is with Allah and losing hope in what is in the hands of people.

f: Why is tawakkul considered a comprehensive spiritual station?
b: Tawakkul combines aspects of fiqh, creed, and spiritual purification, and it requires sincere spiritual training to perfect.

f: What is the Naqshbandī ṭarīqah according to Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ghumuqī?
b: The Naqshbandī ṭarīqah is continuous servitude to Allah through the constant illumination of acts of obedience, especially the remembrance (dhikr) of Allah with the agreement of the heart and tongue.

f: What does the name "Naqshband" mean?
b: "Naqshband" is composed of two Persian words meaning "engraving" and "heart." It refers to engraving the remembrance, love, sincerity, and awareness of Allah upon the heart so that they never leave it.

f: How did Mawlānā Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Dāghistānī explain the meaning of "Naqshband"?
b: He explained it as engraving the Name of Allah upon the heart and acting according to it, so that it produces love, remembrance, righteous conduct, following the Sunnah, and obedience, until the remembrance never disappears from the heart.

f: What are the adab (etiquettes) of the Naqshbandī ṭarīqah?
b: Its etiquettes include: firmly adhering to the Qur'an and Sunnah; having correct creed according to Ahl al-Sunnah; sincere repentance; restoring people's rights and seeking their pardon; constant worship according to the Sunnah; precise adherence to the Sharīʿah; avoiding all sins, evils, and innovations (bidʿah); and maintaining protective concern (ghayrah) for the religion.

f: What is meant by adab in the context of the Naqshbandī ṭarīqah?
b: Adab refers to the principles and disciplines that train and refine the soul, ensuring that one's conduct conforms as completely as possible to the Sharīʿah and the Sunnah.

f: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise for practicing the religion during times when people follow greed, desires, worldly interests, and personal opinions?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said that practicing the religion during such times is like holding a burning coal, and the one who does so will receive the reward of fifty men from among the Prophet's ﷺ Companions.

f: What reward is mentioned for holding firmly to the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah when the Ummah has become corrupt?
b: One narration states that such a person receives the reward of a martyr, while another narration states the reward of one hundred martyrs.

f: What does the term "Book" (الْكِتَابِ) refer to in the expression "the Book and the Sunnah"?
b: It refers to the Noble Qur'an.

f: How do the scholars of ḥadīth define the Sunnah?
b: The Sunnah includes everything transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ, including his sayings, actions, tacit approvals, physical characteristics, character, and biography, whether before or after Prophethood.

f: How do the scholars of uṣūl al-fiqh define the Sunnah?
b: The Sunnah is whatever is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ of his sayings, actions, and tacit approvals. It may also include what is established by a Sharʿī proof from the Qur'an, the Prophet ﷺ, or the ijtihād of the Companions, since uṣūl scholars are concerned with legal proofs.

f: How do the jurists (fuqahāʾ) define the Sunnah?
b: The Sunnah is what is established from the Prophet ﷺ without being obligatory. It is one of the five legal rulings and is often contrasted with bidʿah (innovation).

f: What is the fullest meaning of following the Sunnah?
b: It is following the entirety of what the Prophet ﷺ brought as guidance and methodology, encompassing the meanings emphasized by the scholars of ḥadīth, uṣūl al-fiqh, and fiqh.

f: What is meant by adhering to Ahl al-Sunnah in matters of fiqh?
b: It means adhering to one of the four Sunni schools of law—Ḥanafī, Mālikī, Shāfiʿī, or Ḥanbalī—in matters of worship and legal transactions.

f: How should a seeker treat acts of determination (ʿazīmah)?
b: Every act of determination should be treated like an obligation and should not be abandoned except in cases of compelling necessity.

f: How should a seeker treat legal concessions (rukhaṣ)?
b: Legal concessions should be treated like prohibited matters and should only be taken when genuine necessity requires them.

f: What approach should a seeker adopt in all religious matters?
b: The seeker should always choose the more precautionary opinion (الْأَحْوَطِ).

f: Why should a seeker adopt the more precautionary course and avoid unnecessary concessions?
b: Because doing so is part of venerating Allah's sacred symbols (شَعَائِرُ اللَّهِ), which is a sign of piety, and follows the example of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions in striving for the highest level of obedience and worship.

f: If two acts of worship are equal in virtue, conditions, Sunnahs, and pillars, but one is more difficult than the other, which receives the greater reward?
b: They are equal in reward for the act itself, since they are equal in all required aspects. The additional reward is for patiently bearing the extra hardship for Allah's sake, not for the hardship itself.

f: Why is hardship itself not an act of worship or a means of drawing near to Allah?
b: Because acts of worship consist of honoring and venerating Allah, whereas hardship in itself is neither veneration nor an act of devotion.

f: What did al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām say about the reward of enduring hardship in worship?
b: He said that a person is rewarded for enduring hardship for Allah's sake, not for the hardship itself.

f: When giving legal rulings between two permissible options, which should a scholar recommend?
b: A scholar should recommend the easier option, not the more difficult one.

f: Which ḥadīths support choosing the easier of two permissible options?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away." ʿĀʾishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا also said that whenever the Prophet ﷺ was given a choice between two matters, he chose the easier one so long as it was not sinful.

f: Why should scholars generally recommend the easier permissible option to others?
b: Because others may not be capable of performing the greater level of devotion that the scholar himself is able to undertake.

f: What principle did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding doubtful matters (الشُّبُهَاتِ)?
b: Whoever avoids doubtful matters protects his religion and honor, while whoever falls into doubtful matters is likely to fall into the unlawful.

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about leaving doubtful matters?
b: He said: "Leave what causes you doubt for what does not cause you doubt, for truth brings reassurance while falsehood brings doubt."

f: How did Mūsā ibn Aʿyan explain the verse, "Allah only accepts from the God-fearing" (Qur'an 5:27)?
b: He said that the God-fearing are those who avoid even some lawful matters out of fear of falling into the unlawful.

f: What additional etiquettes of the Naqshbandī path are mentioned after taking the precautionary course?
b: A seeker should avoid destructive blameworthy traits, acquire praiseworthy character, avoid excessive speech, excessive eating, excessive sleeping, and eat only lawful (ḥalāl) food.

f: Why is eating lawful (ḥalāl) food emphasized?
b: Because Allah commands His servants and His messengers to eat what is lawful and pure, and unlawful food is a cause for one's supplications to be rejected.

f: What example did the Prophet ﷺ give of how unlawful earnings affect supplication?
b: He described a traveler who earnestly calls upon Allah while his food, drink, clothing, and nourishment are unlawful, then said: "How can his supplication be answered?"

f: What is meant by maintaining constant poverty before Allah (دَوَامُ الِافْتِقَارِ إِلَى اللَّهِ) together with humility and seeking refuge in Him?
b: It means continually recognizing one's complete need for Allah, humbling oneself before Him, and turning to Him for help in every matter.

f: Which Qur'anic verse teaches mankind's complete dependence upon Allah?
b: "O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah, whereas Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy." (Qur'an 35:15)

f: What are the three signs of divine success (tawfīq)?
b: 1. Good deeds come to a person without deliberately seeking them. 2. Sins are kept away from him despite his inclinations. 3. Allah opens for him the door of seeking refuge in and expressing need before Him in both hardship and ease.

f: What are the three signs of divine abandonment (khidhlān)?
b: 1. Good deeds become difficult despite seeking them. 2. Sins become easy despite trying to avoid them. 3. The door of seeking refuge in and expressing need before Allah is closed.

f: According to al-Dhahabī, upon which two foundations does true servitude ('ubūdiyyah) rest?
b: Complete love for Allah together with complete humility and submission before Him.

f: Why is directing one's complete love and humility to other than Allah considered blameworthy?
b: Because complete love, humility, and submission are Allah's exclusive rights, and giving them to others resembles associating partners with Him.

f: What is meant by cutting off hope from the abode of deception (قَطْعُ الطَّمَعِ عَنْ دَارِ الْغُرُورِ)?
b: It means removing attachment and expectation from worldly life so that the heart relies upon Allah alone.

f: What is meant by being content with Allah's decree (الرِّضَا بِالْمَقْدُورِ)?
b: It means accepting whatever Allah decrees with satisfaction, trusting His wisdom, and not objecting to His judgment.

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach about the relationship between trials and reward?
b: "The greatness of the reward is with the greatness of the trial. When Allah loves a people, He tests them. Whoever is content will have His pleasure, and whoever is displeased will have His displeasure."

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach about contentment with one's allotted provision?
b: Whoever is content with what Allah has apportioned for him will receive blessing in it, while whoever is discontent will neither receive blessing nor obtain more than what Allah has already decreed.

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah for regarding contentment in his famous supplication?
b: He asked Allah for contentment with His decree, the sweetness of life after death, the delight of gazing upon His Face, longing to meet Him, protection from harmful trials, and adornment with faith.

f: How did Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ demonstrate contentment with Allah's decree after losing his eyesight?
b: Although his supplications were accepted and people sought his du'ā, he did not ask Allah to restore his eyesight because he loved Allah's decree more than having his sight returned.

f: What is the promised result for one who observes all of these spiritual etiquettes?
b: He will reach closeness to the Lord of all lords (Allah).

f: What does it indicate if someone performs abundant dhikr of the testimony of faith (kalimat al-tawḥīd) but does not experience its spiritual fruits?
b: It indicates that he has fallen short in observing one or more of the required spiritual etiquettes (ādāb).

f: Why can even a minor breach of spiritual etiquette prevent spiritual progress?
b: Because even a slight violation of adab weakens or prevents the special spiritual effects and benefits of the path.

f: For what intention is it permissible to give bay'ah (the pledge) to a shaykh, spiritual guide, or scholar?
b: It is permissible only with the intention of committing oneself to spiritual purification (tazkiyah) and renewing the covenant to act according to the Qur'an and Sunnah before him as an heir to the Prophet's ﷺ knowledge.

f: Why may a shaykh or scholar receive a pledge of allegiance for spiritual training?
b: Because he is an heir to the knowledge left by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets."

f: Did Imam 'Abd al-Wahhāb al-Sha'rānī write about taking covenants to practice the Sunnah?
b: Yes. In Lawāqiḥ al-Anwār al-Qudsiyyah fī Bayān al-'Uhūd al-Muḥammadiyyah, he records covenants to practice the commands, prohibitions, and etiquettes taught by the Prophet ﷺ.

f: Is it permissible to give a political bay'ah (pledge of rulership) to a shaykh or scholar personally?
b: No. A political pledge belongs only to the legitimate ruler, unless the shaykh or scholar has been formally authorized to act on the ruler's behalf.

f: According to the text, who may receive a political pledge of allegiance (bay'ah al-imāmah)?
b: Only the legitimate ruler, or someone officially appointed to represent him.

f: Between whom are contractual pledges made in ordinary transactions?
b: They are made directly between the parties involved, such as in commercial agreements and marriage contracts.

f: Does the Qur'an establish the concepts of covenant ('ahd), pledge (bay'ah), and covenant (mīthāq)?
b: Yes. The Qur'an repeatedly mentions covenants, pledges, and solemn agreements in various forms and contexts.

f: From whom did Allah take a covenant among the prophets according to the Qur'an?
b: Allah took a covenant from all the prophets, and He especially emphasized the covenant with the greatest messengers (Ulū al-'Azm).

f: Did Allah take covenants from Banī Isrā'īl according to the Qur'an?
b: Yes. Allah took covenants from the Children of Israel regarding worship, righteous conduct, prayer, zakāh, and other obligations.

f: Did Allah take pledges from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Yes. The Qur'an mentions several forms of pledges and covenants taken from the Companions.

f: Does the Qur'an require Muslims to fulfill their covenants even with non-Muslims?
b: Yes. Muslims are commanded to fulfill their treaties and agreements with non-Muslims as long as the other party remains faithful to them.

f: What does Allah say about those who pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ under the tree?
b: Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance under the tree, knew what was in their hearts, sent down tranquility upon them, and rewarded them with a near victory. (Qur'an 48:18)

f: What does the Qur'an say about those who pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ?
b: "Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The Hand of Allah is over their hands." (Qur'an 48:10)

f: What does the Qur'an say about breaking a pledge made to Allah?
b: Whoever breaks the pledge only harms himself, while whoever fulfills his covenant with Allah will receive a tremendous reward. (Qur'an 48:10)

f: What does the Qur'an say about the believers who remained true to their covenant with Allah?
b: Among the believers are men who fulfilled their covenant with Allah; some have completed their duty, others are waiting, and they have never changed their commitment. (Qur'an 33:23)

f: Upon what conditions did the Prophet ﷺ accept the pledge of believing women?
b: They pledged not to associate partners with Allah, not to steal, commit adultery, kill their children, fabricate slander, or disobey him in what is right.

f: How does the Qur'an describe those who fulfill Allah's covenant?
b: They are those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the pledge. (Qur'an 13:20)

f: How should all of Allah's commands and prohibitions be viewed with respect to the covenant?
b: Every command and prohibition is itself a covenant requiring obedience, such as the command to worship Allah sincerely, establish prayer, and give zakāh.

f: Why did the wording of the Prophet's ﷺ pledges of allegiance (bay'ah) differ?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ took pledges according to the need of the occasion, either to renew a covenant or to emphasize a particular obligation.

f: Did the Prophet ﷺ take both general and specific pledges of allegiance?
b: Yes. He took general pledges, such as the First and Second Pledges of al-'Aqabah and the Pledge of al-Riḍwān, as well as specific pledges concerning particular duties.

f: Upon what did Jarīr ibn 'Abd Allāh pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ?
b: To establish the prayer, pay zakāh, and sincerely advise every Muslim.

f: Upon what did 'Ubādah ibn al-Ṣāmit pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Not to associate partners with Allah, not to steal, commit adultery, kill children, fabricate slander, or disobey the Prophet ﷺ in what is right.

f: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise to those who fulfilled the pledge mentioned by 'Ubādah ibn al-Ṣāmit?
b: Whoever fulfilled it would have his reward with Allah. Whoever committed one of those sins and was punished in this world would have it as an expiation, and whoever was concealed by Allah would remain under Allah's judgment.

f: Upon what did Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ?
b: He pledged not to fall except while standing (i.e., to maintain steadfastness and dignity).

f: What commercial principle did the Prophet ﷺ teach Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām after his pledge?
b: "Do not sell what you do not possess."

f: Upon what did Salmā bint Qays and the women of the Anṣār pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Among the conditions was that they would not deceive their husbands.

f: How did the Prophet ﷺ explain "not deceiving one's husband" when asked by the women?
b: He explained that it included giving away or gifting the husband's wealth without his permission.

f: Which virtues did 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān mention while under siege as evidence of his faithfulness?
b: He embraced Islam early, married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ, pledged allegiance with his right hand, maintained chastity, never sang immoral songs, never drank wine in the pre-Islamic period or Islam, and purchased land to expand the Prophet's ﷺ Mosque.

f: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise for purchasing land to expand the mosque?
b: Whoever purchased that land and added it to the mosque would have a house in Paradise.

f: What lesson was learned from the woman who believed she would never be punished because she had fulfilled her pledge to the Prophet ﷺ?
b: She was reminded in a dream that sins such as speaking about what does not concern her and withholding what she should give could still incur accountability, so she repented.

f: Is fulfilling the formal conditions of the bay'ah alone a guarantee against punishment?
b: No. A person must also avoid other sins and continue seeking Allah's forgiveness and repentance.

f: Was the Prophet ﷺ's bay'ah limited to adult men and women?
