f: What should the seeker do after emerging from deep absorption during dhikr?
b: The seeker resumes the remembrance of Allah until the prescribed session is complete.

f: What is recommended immediately after completing the dhikr session?
b: After stopping the dhikr, the seeker remains quietly for a short time, maintaining awareness of the heart while waiting attentively for any spiritual inspirations or blessings (waridāt).

f: Why does the manual advise not opening the eyes immediately after dhikr?
b: Because subtle spiritual blessings or inspirations may descend during those quiet moments, and remaining inwardly attentive may allow the seeker to receive them.

f: Which form of dhikr does the manual describe as superior according to the cited scholars?
b: Dhikr performed with both heart and tongue together is considered best; dhikr of the heart alone comes next, followed by dhikr of the tongue alone.

f: According to Ibn al-Qayyim, why is remembrance of the heart superior to remembrance of the tongue alone?
b: Heart-based remembrance cultivates knowledge of Allah, love, reverence, modesty, fear of Him, vigilance, and greater obedience, whereas remembrance by the tongue alone produces much weaker effects. Ibn al-Qayyim

f: How does the Naqshbandi manual describe the method of beginning silent dhikr with the Divine Name?
b: The seeker closes the lips, places the teeth together, presses the tongue against the roof of the mouth, breathes naturally, and continually imagines the Divine Name Allah within the heart while contemplating Allah's pure Essence without considering His attributes or other Names.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, what should a seeker do if distracted thoughts arise during dhikr?
b: If the seeker becomes distracted or thoughts of anything other than Allah arise, they should immediately seek forgiveness (istighfār) and humbly turn back to Allah, abandoning attachment to everything besides Him.

f: What effect does persistent heart-based dhikr eventually have on awareness of worldly things?
b: Continuous dhikr causes forgetfulness of everything other than the One being remembered (Allah), as the heart becomes increasingly absorbed in His remembrance.

f: When is dhikr said to become firmly established in the heart?
b: Dhikr is firmly established when awareness of Allah becomes a permanent habit (malakah), such that even deliberate attempts to think about something else fail to distract the heart.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, through which subtle faculties does dhikr progress after becoming established in the heart?
b: The manual states that dhikr progresses from the heart (qalb) to the spirit (rūḥ), then to the secret (sirr), then the hidden (khafī), then the most hidden (akhfā), and finally to the rational soul (al-nafs al-nāṭiqah) located in the brain.

f: What are the "secret" (sirr), "hidden" (khafī), and "most hidden" (akhfā) mentioned in the Naqshbandi manual?
b: They are subtle levels of the human inner being used in Sufi terminology to describe progressively deeper dimensions of spiritual awareness. The author relates them to the Qur'anic verse: "He knows the secret and what is even more hidden" (Qur'an 20:7).

f: How did early Qur'anic commentators explain the phrase "the secret and what is more hidden" (السِّرِّ وَأَخْفَى)?
b: Reports from early exegetes explain "the secret" as what a person currently conceals within themselves, while "what is more hidden" refers to matters that Allah knows a person will later think or conceal, even before the person is aware of them.

f: What is meant by "the sovereignty of dhikr" (سُلْطَانُ الذِّكْرِ) in the Naqshbandi manual?
b: It refers to the stage at which remembrance becomes so dominant that it permeates the seeker's entire being.

f: How does the manual describe the experience of the "sovereignty of dhikr"?
b: It describes the seeker as perceiving that every part of their body is engaged in remembering Allah through the Divine Name.

f: How does the Naqshbandi manual describe the seeker's perception of creation after the "sovereignty of dhikr" is attained?
b: It states that the seeker perceives all created things—such as stones, trees, and other creatures—as engaged in glorifying or remembering Allah.

f: What practice does the Naqshbandi manual say follows attainment of the "sovereignty of dhikr"?
b: After reaching this stage, the seeker is instructed by a qualified spiritual guide to begin the dhikr of negation and affirmation (lā ilāha illā Allāh) together with breath retention, according to the method of the order.

f: What is meant by "the sovereignty of dhikr" (سُلْطَانُ الذِّكْرِ) in the Naqshbandi manual?
b: It is the stage at which remembrance of Allah becomes so dominant that it permeates the seeker's entire being and overcomes all other states of awareness.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, what happens when dhikr reaches the rational soul (nafs al-nāṭiqah)?
b: Once dhikr becomes firmly established in the rational soul, the seeker is said to attain the "sovereignty of dhikr," meaning that remembrance completely dominates the person's inner state.

f: How does the Naqshbandi manual describe the effect of the "sovereignty of dhikr" on the seeker's body?
b: The manual states that the seeker perceives every part of the body as participating in the remembrance of Allah, as though the entire body is repeating the Divine Name "Allah."

f: How does the Naqshbandi manual describe the seeker's perception of creation after attaining the "sovereignty of dhikr"?
b: It states that the seeker comes to perceive all created things—stones, trees, earth, and other objects—as engaged in the remembrance or glorification of Allah.

f: Does the Naqshbandi manual present the perception of all creation remembering Allah as an objective claim about creation or as part of the seeker's spiritual experience?
b: The passage presents it as a description of the seeker's spiritual perception and experience after remembrance has become dominant. It does not argue for it philosophically but describes it phenomenologically from within the Sufi path.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, what spiritual practice follows the attainment of the "sovereignty of dhikr"?
b: At that stage, the seeker receives instruction from a qualified spiritual guide in the dhikr of negation and affirmation (lā ilāha illā Allāh) performed together with breath retention.

f: How did early Qur'anic commentators explain the phrase "the secret and what is more hidden" (السِّرِّ وَأَخْفَى) in Qur'an 20:7?
b: Early commentators offered several explanations: (1) the secret is what a person currently conceals, while the more hidden is what Allah knows they will later think before they know it themselves; (2) the secret refers to hidden actions, while the more hidden refers to inner whispers (waswasah); (3) the secret is a settled intention, while the more hidden is a passing thought that has not yet become a firm resolve.

f: How did Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī explain "the secret and what is more hidden" (Qur'an 20:7)?
b: Al-Rāzī explained that Allah's knowledge encompasses three levels: what is spoken openly, what is secretly resolved within the heart, and what is even subtler than that—such as thoughts that have not yet become firm intentions or matters known only to Allah before they occur. He says this emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and encourages sincerity by reminding people that both hidden obedience and hidden sin are known to Him.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, what are the two general categories of seekers regarding their worldly circumstances?
b: The manual divides seekers into (1) those who are detached from family responsibilities (single or free from worldly obligations) and (2) those who have families, dependents, or occupations.

f: What does the Naqshbandi manual recommend for a seeker who is free from family responsibilities?
b: Such a seeker is advised to follow the stricter path (ʿazīmah): withdraw from worldly distractions as much as possible, prefer seclusion over unnecessary socializing, while still maintaining obligatory communal religious duties such as Jumuʿah and congregational prayer.

f: Does the Naqshbandi manual permit complete isolation from the Muslim community?
b: No. Even when recommending seclusion, it explicitly requires preserving obligations such as Friday prayer and congregational prayer.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, which acts of worship should a detached seeker prioritize?
b: The seeker should fulfill the obligatory acts, the emphasized Sunnah prayers, and the regular Sunnah prayers, while giving priority to continuous dhikr over additional voluntary acts of worship until constant presence of heart with Allah is attained.

f: Why does the Naqshbandi manual recommend prioritizing dhikr over additional voluntary worship for some seekers?
b: It explains that the primary work of the Sufi path is combating distracting thoughts, refining character, and removing heedlessness from the heart. After fulfilling obligatory and emphasized Sunnah acts, sustained dhikr is considered more beneficial for achieving those aims than increasing optional devotional acts.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, when should a seeker increase optional prayers and other voluntary acts?
b: After the heart has been purified from blameworthy qualities and constant presence with Allah has become established, the seeker is then encouraged to engage freely in all forms of voluntary worship.

f: What should a seeker do if spiritual fatigue or lack of motivation occurs during dhikr?
b: Rather than remaining idle, the seeker should temporarily occupy the time with another act of worship—such as prayer, Qur'an recitation, or vocal dhikr—until spiritual energy returns, then resume the primary practice of dhikr as soon as possible.

f: Does the Naqshbandi manual permit abandoning dhikr for long periods because of spiritual dryness?
b: No. It recommends only a temporary change of devotional activity until enthusiasm returns, after which the seeker should immediately resume the prescribed dhikr.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, during which daily activities should awareness of Allah be maintained?
b: The seeker should strive to maintain inner vigilance and awareness of Allah while speaking with people, keeping company, conducting business, fulfilling personal needs, performing acts of worship, being alone, going to sleep, and even during sleep whenever possible.

f: Does the Naqshbandi manual describe continuous awareness of Allah as easy to attain?
b: No. It emphasizes that this state is achieved only through disciplining the ego (nafs), resisting its desires, and consistently striving against it.

f: How does the Naqshbandi manual describe the value of time for the spiritual seeker?
b: It urges the seeker not to waste even a single moment, quoting the well-known maxim: "Time is a cutting sword; if you do not cut with it, it will cut you."

f: What guidance does the Naqshbandi manual give to seekers who have families or occupations?
b: Those with worldly responsibilities are instructed to follow the easier path (rukhṣah), adapting the spiritual program to their circumstances while continuing their responsibilities rather than withdrawing from society.

f: What famous sayings are attributed to al-Shāfiʿī regarding the wisdom he learned from the Sufis?
b: He is reported to have said that he benefited from the Sufis by learning three maxims: (1) "Time is a sword; if you do not cut with it, it will cut you." (2) "If you do not occupy your soul with truth, it will occupy you with falsehood." (3) "Nonexistence (or withdrawal) is protection." (The authenticity of this attribution is a matter of scholarly discussion.)

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, what morning routine is recommended for a seeker with family or worldly responsibilities?
b: After praying Ṣalāt al-Fajr and reciting Sūrat Yā Sīn, the seeker should engage in silent contemplation (murāqabah) until the sun has risen approximately one or two spear-lengths above the horizon.

f: When should the Ishrāq prayer be performed according to the Naqshbandi manual?
b: It should be performed after the sun has risen roughly one or two spear-lengths above the horizon following Fajr.

f: How many rakʿahs does the Naqshbandi manual prescribe for the Ishrāq prayer?
b: It recommends praying two rakʿahs.

f: Which sūrahs does the Naqshbandi manual recommend reciting in the two rakʿahs of Ishrāq?
b: It recommends Sūrat al-Kāfirūn in the first rakʿah and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ in the second.

f: What prayer does the Naqshbandi manual recommend immediately after the Ishrāq prayer?
b: It recommends praying two rakʿahs of Ṣalāt al-Istikhārah.

f: How does the Naqshbandi manual describe the purpose of performing a daily Istikhārah prayer?
b: Citing Muḥyī al-Dīn Ibn ʿArabī, it explains that one performs two rakʿahs intending to seek Allah's guidance for every movement and every period of stillness during the coming day (or another chosen period), asking that all one's actions be directed toward what is best.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, what is hoped for by performing this comprehensive Istikhārah?
b: The hope is that every action affecting the seeker—or occurring to the seeker through others—during the intended period will be guided toward what is good by Allah's permission.

f: What supplication does the Naqshbandi manual recommend after the two rakʿahs of Istikhārah?
b: It recommends reciting the well-known duʿāʾ of Istikhārah, beginning: "Allāhumma innī astakhīruka bi-ʿilmik, wa astaqdiruka bi-qudratik..." ("O Allah, I seek the better by Your knowledge, seek strength through Your power, and ask You from Your immense bounty...").

f: What authentic hadiths are cited regarding remaining in remembrance after Fajr until sunrise?
b: The notes cite hadiths stating that one who remains remembering Allah after Fajr until sunrise and then prays two rakʿahs receives a reward comparable to an accepted Hajj and ʿUmrah, and that the Prophet ﷺ would remain in his place after Fajr until the sun rose.

f: What comprehensive intention does the Naqshbandi manual recommend making in the duʿāʾ of Istikhārah?
b: The seeker asks Allah to decree and facilitate whatever movements, stillness, actions, and affairs from that moment onward are best for the seeker's religion, worldly life, and ultimate outcome, and to turn away whatever is harmful.

f: After completing the morning adhkār and Istikhārah, what should the seeker do according to the Naqshbandi manual?
b: The seeker should go about earning a livelihood and fulfilling worldly responsibilities while striving to maintain inward awareness of Allah and continual remembrance of Him.

f: How does the Naqshbandi manual reconcile worldly work with constant remembrance of Allah?
b: It teaches that earning a livelihood should not distract the heart from Allah, citing the Qur'anic description of believers: "Men whom neither trade nor commerce distracts from the remembrance of Allah." (Qur'an 24:37).

f: What does the Sufi expression "khalwah fi al-jalwah" (الْخَلْوَةُ فِي الْجَلْوَةِ) mean according to the commentary?
b: It means being outwardly among people while inwardly remaining with Allah—maintaining inward remembrance and presence with Allah even while working, interacting with others, and fulfilling daily responsibilities.

f: How did Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz describe the spiritually complete person?
b: He described the complete person as someone who buys, sells, marries, and mixes with people while never becoming heedless of Allah, even for a single moment. Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz

f: What does the Naqshbandi manual recommend after completing one's worldly work?
b: After finishing one's responsibilities, the seeker should enter seclusion, perform wudu, pray two rakʿahs, and then resume the prescribed spiritual practices (wird).

f: Which prayer is recommended after the period of seclusion later in the morning?
b: The manual recommends performing Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā, consisting of between two and twelve rakʿahs.

f: According to the Naqshbandi manual, what should the seeker do after praying Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā?
b: The seeker should take the qaylūlah (a midday nap or rest) before continuing the day's schedule.

f: What is the recommended practice before the Ẓuhr prayer according to the Naqshbandi manual?
b: The seeker should arrive at the mosque at the beginning of the time for Ẓuhr. If worldly duties remain, they should complete them; otherwise, they should continue their prescribed dhikr and spiritual exercises.

f: What does the Naqshbandi manual recommend before the ʿAṣr prayer?
b: The seeker should attend the mosque at the beginning of the time for ʿAṣr.

f: Why does the Naqshbandi manual place special importance on the period between ʿAṣr and Maghrib?
b: It describes safeguarding the time between ʿAṣr and Maghrib as one of the most important spiritual practices, encouraging the seeker to avoid wasting it and instead occupy it with remembrance of Allah.

f: How should the seeker spend the time between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ according to the Naqshbandi manual?
b: The seeker should likewise avoid wasting this period and continue with the prescribed inward dhikr and spiritual exercises.

f: What practice is recommended after Ṣalāt al-Awwābīn according to the Naqshbandi manual?
b: After praying Ṣalāt al-Awwābīn, the seeker should continue the inward (heart-based) dhikr and prescribed spiritual practices.

f: What hadiths are cited regarding the virtue of praying two rakʿahs after wudu?
b: The commentary cites the hadith that whoever performs wudu properly and then prays two rakʿahs with full concentration has previous sins forgiven, and the hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ praised Bilāl ibn Rabāḥ for consistently praying after every wudu.

f: What range of rakʿahs for Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā does the commentary mention?
b: It notes reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed four, eight, and other numbers of rakʿahs, explaining that two to twelve rakʿahs are all acceptable based on the relevant narrations.

f: Which Qur'anic verses are cited to emphasize remembrance of Allah during the morning and evening?
b: The commentary cites Qur'an 33:41–42 ("Remember Allah with much remembrance...") and Qur'an 7:205, which commands remembering Allah morning and evening without heedlessness.

f: What hadith is cited regarding Ṣalāt al-Awwābīn after Maghrib?
b: The commentary cites a narration stating that whoever prays six rakʿahs after Maghrib without engaging in sinful speech between them receives the reward of twelve years of worship, though scholars differ regarding the strength of this report.

f: What nightly routine is recommended after the ʿIshāʾ prayer?
b: After ʿIshāʾ, recite Sūrat al-Mulk. If not occupied with the spiritual wird, recite Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, al-Muʿawwidhatayn (Sūrat al-Falaq and Sūrat al-Nās), and the last verses of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, all with presence of heart.

f: What supplication should be recited three times before sleeping?
b: "Astaghfirullāha alladhī lā ilāha illā huwa al-Ḥayyu al-Qayyūmu wa-atūbu ilayh." ("I seek forgiveness from Allah, besides Whom there is no deity, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I repent to Him.")

f: In what spiritual state should a seeker go to sleep?
b: The seeker should sleep while maintaining awareness of the inner (silent) remembrance (dhikr).

f: When should Tahajjud be prayed?
b: Tahajjud should be performed after sleeping, not before sleeping. Prayer before sleep counts as Qiyām al-Layl, but not Tahajjud. Some also described Tahajjud as occurring between two periods of sleep.

f: What sleeping practice is recommended after Tahajjud?
b: It is recommended to take a light sleep after Tahajjud, although one should strive to rise for it as early as possible during the night.

f: How are the different portions of the night characterized spiritually?
b: The early part of the night is the state of the worshippers (al-ʿābidīn), the middle of the night is the state of the devoutly obedient (al-qānitīn), and the later part of the night is regarded as the most distinguished time for night worship.

f: How should Sūrat Yā Sīn be divided across the eight rakʿahs of Tahajjud?
b: The first rakʿah is recited up to ﴿وَأَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾, the second up to ﴿وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾, the third up to ﴿جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضِرُونَ﴾, the fourth up to ﴿وَكُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾, the fifth up to ﴿وَإِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾, the sixth up to ﴿صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾, the seventh up to ﴿فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ﴾, and the eighth completes the remainder of the sūrah.

f: What should be recited in the remaining rakʿahs after completing the portions of Sūrat Yā Sīn?
b: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ should be recited three times in each remaining rakʿah.

f: What should someone do if they have not memorized Sūrat Yā Sīn?
b: They should recite Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ three times in every rakʿah instead.

f: What should a seeker do after completing the Tahajjud prayer?
b: After finishing the prayer, the seeker should remain seated in the Tahajjud posture and continue the inner (silent) dhikr (wird) until Fajr. If overcome by sleep, they may sleep briefly, then wake for Fajr.

f: What should a seeker do before and after going to the mosque for Fajr?
b: They should pray the two rakʿahs of Sunnah before Fajr at home, occupy themselves with istighfār while going to the mosque, and after praying Fajr in congregation, continue their prescribed spiritual wird.

f: What are the two Naqshbandī methods of dhikr?
b: The two methods are the dhikr of the Divine Name (Ism al-Dhāt, "Allah") and the dhikr of negation and affirmation ("Lā ilāha illā Allāh").

f: Which type of seeker is best suited to the dhikr of the Divine Name (Ism al-Dhāt)?
b: The dhikr of the Divine Name is for one naturally disposed to receiving jadhbah (spiritual attraction).

f: Which type of seeker is best suited to the dhikr of negation and affirmation (Lā ilāha illā Allāh)?
b: The dhikr of negation and affirmation is for one naturally disposed to sulūk (gradual spiritual wayfaring), and it is performed with the heart.

f: How is the Naqshbandī dhikr of negation and affirmation (Lā ilāha illā Allāh) performed?
b: The tongue is pressed against the roof of the mouth as in the dhikr of the Divine Name, the breath is held, and the phrase "Lā ilāha illā Allāh" is visualized moving through specific points of the body while concentrating on its meaning.

f: During the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh, how is the phrase "Lā" visualized?
b: "Lā" is visualized as beginning below the navel and ascending until it reaches the brain.

f: During the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh, how is the phrase "Ilāha" visualized?
b: "Ilāha" is visualized as moving from the brain to the right shoulder.

f: During the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh, how is the phrase "Illā Allāh" visualized?
b: "Illā Allāh" is visualized as extending from the right shoulder across the chest to the physical heart on the left side, where the Divine Name is struck forcefully until its spiritual warmth is felt throughout the body and all the subtle faculties (laṭāʾif).

f: What meaning should be contemplated while performing the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh?
b: The seeker should contemplate that there is no true object of desire or aim except Allah. Through the negation (Lā ilāha), everything other than Allah is negated and viewed with the eye of annihilation (fanāʾ); through the affirmation (Illā Allāh), the reality of Allah alone is affirmed and contemplated with the eye of abiding (baqāʾ).

f: What is visualized with the phrase "Muḥammad Rasūl Allāh" after completing the dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh?
b: The phrase "Muḥammad Rasūl Allāh" is visualized as proceeding from the heart toward the right side, completing the remembrance.

f: What does the visualization of "Muḥammad Rasūl Allāh" represent in the Naqshbandī dhikr of negation and affirmation?
b: It represents following (ittibāʿ) and love for the Prophet ﷺ.

f: When should the breath be released during the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh?
b: The breath should be released only when necessary, at which point the seeker says: "Ilāhī anta maqṣūdī wa-riḍāka maṭlūbī" ("My God, You are my goal, and Your pleasure is what I seek.").

f: How should the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh appear outwardly?
b: It should be performed without any visible bodily movement, so that even someone nearby does not perceive it.

f: What should a seeker do between breaths while performing the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh?
b: Between breaths, the seeker should maintain the same inner visualization without becoming heedless, preserving continuity before beginning the next breath.

f: How should the number of repetitions per breath progress in the Naqshbandī dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh?
b: The seeker begins with one repetition per breath, then three, then gradually increases the number while keeping to odd numbers, until reaching twenty-one repetitions in a single breath.

f: What spiritual result is expected after reaching twenty-one repetitions of Lā ilāha illā Allāh in one breath?
b: The seeker is expected to experience absorption and self-forgetfulness, with the negation removing attachment to human existence and the affirmation producing the effects of Divine attraction (jadhbah), such as forgetting everything besides Allah and returning to Him in humility and brokenness.

f: Why may the expected spiritual results of the Naqshbandī dhikr not appear?
b: They may fail to appear because of deficiencies in observing the required spiritual etiquettes (ādāb). The seeker should renew their striving, ensure that their actions, beliefs, and adherence to the Sunnah match the meaning of the dhikr, and avoid insincerity by making Allah alone their true goal.

f: What stages of spiritual experience may different seekers encounter through the Naqshbandī dhikr?
b: Depending on their spiritual readiness, a seeker may first experience absence from everything besides Allah (ghaybah), or absence together with spiritual intoxication (sukr), then realization of the non-existence of the self, and finally fanāʾ (annihilation of the ego).

f: What must accompany the declaration of faith (Lā ilāha illā Allāh) in practice?
b: It must be accompanied by putting its meaning into practice by removing all improper attachments, sincerely following the Prophet ﷺ, seeking what is lawful and pure, and loving the righteous.

f: What should be contemplated during the negation (Lā ilāha) in the Naqshbandī dhikr of negation and affirmation?
b: During the negation, the seeker should negate the attributes and attachments of human nature.

f: What should be contemplated during the affirmation (Illā Allāh) in the Naqshbandī dhikr of negation and affirmation?
b: During the affirmation, the seeker should contemplate the absolute oneness of the Divine Essence.

f: What should continual presence with Allah and perfect following of the Prophet ﷺ produce?
b: They should produce continuous servitude through self-effacement (istihlāk), manifesting the relationship between Lordship (rubūbiyyah) and servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah), which encompasses nearness to Allah and all spiritual knowledge.

f: How did al-Shiblī describe the value of complete presence of heart with Allah?
b: He said that the presence of his heart while immersed in the light of his Lord was better than the knowledge of all those who came before and after, emphasizing the superiority of direct spiritual presence over mere intellectual knowledge.

f: How does the author describe the ultimate goal of the spiritual path?
b: It is the highest objective of the prophets and messengers: complete absorption in the lights of Allah's beauty and majesty, leading to true nearness to Him and success in this world and the Hereafter.

f: What physical effects may appear when a person consistently remembers Allah with the tongue while directing the heart toward Him?
b: The person may experience pain in the limbs and joints, pain in the heart, and slight perspiration.

f: How does the author explain the cause of the physical discomfort experienced during sustained dhikr?
b: He explains that dhikr cuts away the worldly pleasures and lower desires that had become rooted in the heart and body during periods of heedlessness, marking the beginning of dhikr's penetration into the heart.

f: According to the author, what happens as a seeker continues to persevere in dhikr?
b: The effect of dhikr reaches the spirit (rūḥ), which takes its place upon the throne of the heart, governs the outward and inward faculties, subdues the lower self (nafs), and eventually extends to the secret (sirr) and the remaining subtle faculties (laṭāʾif). This stage is called the "sovereignty of dhikr" (Sulṭān al-Dhikr).

f: What is meant by the "sovereignty of dhikr" (Sulṭān al-Dhikr)?
b: It is the stage at which the effects of dhikr have spread through the heart, spirit, secret, and all the subtle faculties, so that the spirit governs the person and the lower self is subdued.

f: What signs indicate that the effects of dhikr have spread throughout the body?
b: Every limb begins to experience rhythmic pulsations and involuntary movements, which increase with continued dhikr until they may be perceived as sounds or speech.

f: What extraordinary experience does the author say may occur after prolonged perseverance in dhikr?
b: The seeker may hear every part of the body engaged in remembrance of Allah, and even hear the heart uttering Divine Names and forms of dhikr previously unknown, expressed in diverse ways.

f: What qualifies a seeker for the station of murāqabah (spiritual watchfulness)?
b: A seeker becomes qualified for murāqabah after striving in the dhikr of Lā ilāha illā Allāh until the negation and affirmation have fully taken effect, producing self-forgetfulness (dhuhūl) and self-effacement (istihlāk).

f: What is muraqabah (spiritual vigilance) in the Naqshbandi path?
b: Muraqabah is a noble spiritual state and an act of worship in which the seeker maintains continual awareness of Allah. Through it, Allah illuminates the heart with maʿrifah (gnosis), opens the breast to the realities of faith, and brings the seeker closer to Him.

f: What is the linguistic meaning of muraqabah?
b: Muraqabah comes from the root ra-qaf-ba (ر ق ب), meaning to watch, observe, guard, or remain vigilant. A raqīb is a watcher or guardian, and murāqabat Allāh means to remain mindful of Allah and fear Him.

f: What Qur'anic verses establish the principle of muraqabah?
b: The Qur'an repeatedly teaches Allah's constant knowledge and watchfulness, including: "Indeed, Allah is Ever Watchful over you" (4:1), "He is with you wherever you are" (57:4), "Does he not know that Allah sees?" (96:14), and "He knows the secret and what is even more hidden" (20:7).

f: What Prophetic teaching is the foundation of muraqabah?
b: The foundation is the hadith of Jibrīl describing iḥsān: "Worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you."

f: How did Ibn Ḥajar explain iḥsān and muraqabah?
b: He explained that iḥsān consists of sincerity, humility, freedom from distractions in worship, and awareness that Allah constantly sees every action of the servant.

f: How did Imām al-Nawawī explain the purpose of muraqabah?
b: He said its purpose is to encourage sincerity in worship, continual awareness of Allah, complete humility, and excellence in one's acts of devotion.

f: Which hadith links tasting the sweetness of faith with muraqabah?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said that among the qualities of one who tastes the sweetness of faith is "purifying his soul," which he explained as knowing that Allah is with him wherever he is.

f: How did al-Ḥārith al-Muḥāsibī define muraqabah?
b: He defined it as the heart's continual awareness of Allah's knowledge during both movement and stillness, accompanied by certainty and purity of faith.

f: How did Ibn al-Qayyim define muraqabah?
b: He defined it as the servant's continual certainty that Allah constantly observes both his outward actions and his inward state.

f: What spiritual effects does muraqabah produce according to the Naqshbandi tradition?
b: It illuminates the heart with maʿrifah, opens the breast to spiritual realities, strengthens discernment, grants truthful spiritual perception, improves one's conduct with Allah, and perfects one's worship.

f: Why is muraqabah described as one of the greatest acts of worship?
b: Because it is a continuous act of the heart that perfects sincerity and accompanies every other act of worship, making all acts more complete and accepted.

f: What did the righteous predecessors emphasize alongside muraqabah?
b: They devoted themselves to constant muraqabah, prolonged reflection (fikr), and continual remembrance of Lā ilāha illā Allāh, considering these among the greatest means of drawing near to Allah.

f: What saying is mentioned regarding reflection (tafakkur), and what does it mean?
b: It is reported: "A moment of reflection is better than a year of worship." Reflection is considered one of the paths leading to the station of spiritual witnessing (mushāhadah). Whoever perseveres in it may become among those who attain closeness (wusūl).

f: How is muraqabah defined in the Naqshbandi tradition?
b: Muraqabah is maintaining continuous awareness that Allah is observing the servant in every state and condition.

f: What are the conditions for practising muraqabah?
b: The seeker should be physically and spiritually purified, have presence of heart, and sit in a pure place free from distractions, noises, and interruptions.

f: How should the seeker sit when practising muraqabah?
b: The seeker sits on his knees facing the qiblah, closes his eyes, and withdraws his attention from external distractions.

f: What should the seeker do inwardly before beginning muraqabah?
b: He should abandon reliance on his own power and ability, forget worldly knowledge and attachments, quiet his external senses and internal thoughts, and turn completely toward Allah.

f: How should the seeker direct his heart during muraqabah?
b: He should direct his heart completely toward the Divine Essence of Allah, with the attraction and pull of Allah's sustaining power (al-jadhbah al-qayyūmiyyah), while remaining aware of Allah's presence.

f: What does the seeker remove from the heart in muraqabah?
b: He removes everything besides Allah from the heart so that the effect of "illā Allāh" (except Allah) can enter the heart and spread to the limbs.

f: What did Mawlānā Khālid al-Naqshbandī say about removing other than Allah from the heart?
b: He said that the seeker removes everything besides Allah from the heart so that the influence of "illā Allāh" becomes established in the heart and spreads throughout the body.

f: How long should the seeker remain engaged in muraqabah according to this method?
b: The seeker should remain attached to this practice at all times after completing the obligatory prayers and confirmed sunnah prayers until distracting thoughts, attachment to physical desires, and inner disturbances disappear.

f: What spiritual changes occur through continuous muraqabah?
b: Through continuous muraqabah, the soul becomes purified, the temperament becomes balanced, and the spiritual aspect of the seeker becomes dominant over the physical aspect.

f: When is it recommended for the seeker to return to mixing with people?
b: After the state of muraqabah becomes firmly established as a lasting quality within the seeker, it becomes recommended for him to interact with people and engage in additional acts of worship.

f: Why can the seeker perform many types of worship after reaching this level?
b: Because after reaching this spiritual state, the seeker can draw closer to Allah through various acts of worship and understands the ways of receiving divine spiritual benefit (istifādah).

f: What are the conditions of muraqabah?
b: The conditions of muraqabah are that it is practised with the permission, instruction, guidance, and spiritual training of the shaykh; that it is accompanied by the Divine sustaining attraction (al-jadhbah al-qayyūmiyyah); and that it occurs after cutting off sensory and spiritual attachments.

f: What is the relationship between muraqabah and mushāhadah (spiritual witnessing)?
b: Whoever preserves the conditions and manners of muraqabah progresses from muraqabah to mushāhadah, which is the higher station of iḥsān.

f: What are the manners (ādāb) of muraqabah?
b: Its manners include maintaining silence, remaining secluded, restraining the senses from distractions, suspending excessive reliance on intellectual perception, avoiding reading and writing, turning away from following the ego's pursuit of knowledge, opposing desires, abandoning worldly hopes, and leaving every inclination that distracts from Allah.

f: What does istifādah mean in the context of the Naqshbandi path?
b: Istifādah means seeking the arrival of divine spiritual benefit and illumination into the heart through prolonged reflection, muraqabah, and turning toward Allah. It is not meant in the legal sense of proving rights, lineage, marriage, ownership, or similar matters.

f: How does istifādah occur according to this explanation?
b: When the heart is polished through constant remembrance, reflection, and muraqabah, Allah grants the servant forms of knowledge and recognition that are not acquired through ordinary learning, but are divine openings.

f: What are the two levels of iḥsān mentioned in relation to muraqabah and mushāhadah?
b: The highest level of iḥsān is "to worship Allah as though you see Him", which is the station of mushāhadah. The lower level is "if you do not see Him, then He sees you", which is the station of muraqabah.

f: What are the further manners (ādāb) required for the seeker practising muraqabah?
b: The seeker should strive for reaching Allah, maintain constant orientation toward meeting Him, abandon desire for spiritual ranks, avoid seeking miracles (karāmāt), maintain proper etiquette with Allah outwardly and inwardly, and observe Him in all situations.

f: Why does the seeker abandon distractions besides Allah during muraqabah?
b: Because the purpose is to remain occupied with Allah, purify the heart through turning toward Him, and develop constant awareness of Allah's presence. The heart must be cleansed and refined so that muraqabah becomes continuous.

f: Does abandoning distractions mean completely separating from people and worldly activities?
b: No. It does not mean abandoning reading, relationships, or social interaction. Rather, it means correcting one's intention and maintaining awareness of Allah whether alone, in worship, or among people.

f: What is the ideal state of the perfected seeker while living among people?
b: The perfected seeker interacts with people, trades, works, and fulfills worldly responsibilities, while his heart remains attached to Allah and occupied with His remembrance.

f: Which Qur'anic verse describes those whose worldly activities do not distract them from Allah?
b: Allah says: "Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah, nor from establishing prayer and giving zakāh; they fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be overturned." (Qur'an 24:37)

f: What worldly attachments are specifically warned against distracting the believer from Allah?
b: Wealth and children are mentioned as things that can distract a person from Allah's remembrance. Allah says: "O believers, do not let your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. Whoever does so—then they are the losers." (Qur'an 63:9)

f: What example does the Qur'an give of people leaving worship due to worldly attraction?
b: Allah mentions those who, upon seeing trade or entertainment, leave the Prophet ﷺ standing during the sermon to pursue it, and reminds them that what is with Allah is better than entertainment and trade. (Qur'an 62:11)

f: What is the balance between worldly life and muraqabah?
b: The seeker should not abandon lawful worldly responsibilities, but should prevent them from occupying the heart. The outward body may be engaged with creation while the inward heart remains connected to Allah.

f: What is the purpose of the previous practices of heart dhikr, presence, muraqabah, and tawḥīd?
b: They are spiritual preparations to engrave the remembrance of Allah and true orientation toward Him upon the heart until the seeker becomes deeply accustomed to His love, obedience, remembrance, and following what pleases Him.

f: Is the method of purification through heart dhikr easy to achieve?
b: No. It requires effort, discipline, and struggle against the desires of the ego. It is a path of purification through remembrance of Allah and is not achieved effortlessly.

f: Is the intense method of dhikr described for every person?
b: No. The detailed practices of dhikr with specific methods are not required from everyone. Many seekers are only required to maintain the outward obligations of the Sharīʿah, recite Qur'an, perform daily adhkār, observe voluntary worship, and have good character with creation.

f: What is the basic requirement expected from ordinary seekers according to this explanation?
b: They should adhere to the outward Sharīʿah, recite the Qur'an, maintain daily remembrance and voluntary acts of worship, and treat people with good manners and excellent character.

f: What example is given of a person whose heart becomes emptied of everything except Allah?
b: The pilgrim standing at ʿArafah is given as an example. He leaves behind worldly attachments, stands before Allah in humility and brokenness, and presents a heart focused only upon Him.

f: What hadith is mentioned regarding the people of ʿArafah?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than the Day of ʿArafah. He draws near and boasts of them to the angels, saying: What do these people want?"

f: What happens when the seeker's heart reaches a state of complete emptiness from awareness of self and creation?
b: According to this path, the heart receives the beginnings of fanāʾ (spiritual annihilation), including states of absence (ghaybah), spiritual intoxication (sukr), and awareness of the non-existence of created things in comparison to Allah.

f: When does the seeker begin the practice of verbal dhikr with "Lā ilāha illā Allāh"?
b: When the heart reaches these initial states of fanāʾ and becomes prepared through previous spiritual training, the seeker begins verbal dhikr with Lā ilāha illā Allāh.

f: What is the minimum amount of verbal dhikr of "Lā ilāha illā Allāh" mentioned for the seeker?
b: The minimum mentioned for the seeker is five thousand repetitions.

f: Is there a maximum limit to the amount of verbal dhikr?
b: No. There is no maximum limit in terms of numbers, because the highest form of verbal remembrance is to spend all times engaged in dhikr of Allah.

f: Why is verbal dhikr considered important after heart purification?
b: Because after the heart has been prepared through presence, muraqabah, and inner purification, verbal dhikr strengthens and expresses the remembrance of Allah until remembrance becomes continuous.

f: How is the Naqshbandi practice of verbal dhikr with Lā ilāha illā Allāh performed?
b: The seeker recites Lā ilāha illā Allāh without moving his limbs or leaning to the right or left. He begins the phrase lā from above the navel, extends it toward below the right chest, continues with ilāh, then brings illā Allāh from below the right chest and directs it toward the heart.

f: What should the seeker contemplate while reciting Lā ilāha illā Allāh in this practice?
b: The seeker contemplates the meaning: "There is nothing that truly exists except Allah" (lā mawjūda illā Allāh), while directing the remembrance toward the heart.

f: What does complete fanāʾ mean in this spiritual explanation?
b: Complete fanāʾ means that awareness of Allah's command and presence overwhelms the servant's awareness of himself, so that the servant's will becomes completely surrendered to Allah and all matters are referred back to Him.

f: How does a person in the state of fanāʾ relate to his own choices?
b: The servant no longer sees himself as independently acting by his own power and choice; rather, he sees his actions and affairs as dependent upon Allah's will and guidance.

f: What is the first degree of wilayah (spiritual sainthood) described in this passage?
b: The first degree of wilayah is performing obedience to Allah in the most complete manner while being humble, broken-hearted, and fully connected to Allah through heart and thought.

f: How should a person perform acts of worship after spiritual purification?
b: He should perform worship like the pilgrim, worshipper, and supplicant: with continuous awareness of Allah, humility, and the heart and mind directed toward Him.

f: What is the purpose of heart remembrance (dhikr qalbī)?
b: The purpose of heart remembrance is to establish continuous awareness of Allah in the heart and to make the servant constantly oriented toward Him.

f: Does reaching spiritual states require abandoning worldly responsibilities?
b: No. Spiritual purification does not mean abandoning worldly duties; rather, the believer should fulfil responsibilities in creation while maintaining inward attachment to Allah.

f: What responsibility does Islam give humans regarding the earth?
b: Humans are entrusted with the role of khalīfah (vicegerent) on earth, meaning they should cultivate, develop, and manage the world according to Allah's guidance.

f: How should a believer combine worship and worldly excellence?
b: A believer should combine devotion to Allah with striving for strength, knowledge, economic ability, intellectual growth, physical capability, and beneficial contribution to society.

f: What Qur'anic verse is mentioned regarding humanity's role on earth?
b: Allah says: "He created you from the earth and settled you upon it, so seek His forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive." (Qur'an 11:61)

f: What hadith is mentioned about seeking strength and benefit?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah's help, and do not be incapable." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim)

f: What is the meaning of the "minor annihilation" (الْفِنَاءُ الصُّغْرَى) in the Naqshbandi terminology?
b: The minor annihilation is the servant's remaining through Allah after annihilating his own ego. It refers to the state where the servant's self-centered existence and desires are overcome, and he becomes established through obedience, awareness of Allah, and reliance upon Him.

f: What does it mean that the servant "remains by Allah after annihilation of himself" (بَقَاءُ الْعَبْدِ بِالْحَقِّ عِنْدَ الْفِنَاءِ بِنَفْسِهِ)?
b: It means that after the servant's ego, desires, and attachment to himself are overcome, he continues to exist as a servant guided by Allah, acting through obedience to Him rather than through selfish motives.

f: What Quranic evidence is mentioned regarding Allah's friendship (wilayah) with believers?
b: Allah says: "Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light" (Qur'an 2:257).

f: What Quranic verse is mentioned regarding Allah being the protector of the righteous?
b: Allah says: "Indeed, my Protector is Allah, who revealed the Book, and He takes care of the righteous" (Qur'an 7:196).

f: What Quranic verse describes the qualities and reward of Allah's awliyāʾ (friends)?
b: Allah says: "Indeed, the friends of Allah shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve: those who believed and were conscious of Allah. For them are glad tidings in this world and the Hereafter" (Qur'an 10:62-64).

f: How are the awliyāʾ of Allah described in the hadith about people envied by prophets and martyrs?
b: They are servants of Allah who love one another for Allah's sake without ties of wealth or lineage. Their faces are illuminated, they sit upon pulpits of light, and they do not fear when people fear nor grieve when people grieve.

f: What quality causes certain servants of Allah to be envied by prophets and martyrs?
b: Their closeness to Allah, their sincere love for one another for His sake, and their spiritual rank cause them to be envied by prophets and martyrs.

f: What does the hadith "The awliyāʾ of Allah are those who, when seen, Allah is remembered" indicate?
b: It indicates that true friends of Allah possess such a state of nearness and spiritual illumination that their presence reminds people of Allah.

f: What is one sign of the people of Allah mentioned in the hadith of Ibn Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا?
b: A sign of Allah's awliyāʾ is that when people see them, they remember Allah.

f: What does the hadith "The best of you are those who, when seen, Allah is remembered" teach?
b: It teaches that one of the highest qualities of righteous people is that their character, worship, and spiritual state inspire others to remember Allah.

f: What is the spiritual state of the person who has reached minor annihilation according to the Naqshbandi path?
b: He remains connected to Allah while interacting with creation. He is not distracted by creation from Allah, nor does his connection with Allah prevent him from dealing properly with creation.

f: What does it mean that the perfected servant is not veiled by creation from the Creator nor by the Creator from creation?
b: It means he maintains balance: his heart remains attached to Allah while his outward life continues with people, fulfilling responsibilities and interacting with the world.

f: When does the seeker become suited for increasing voluntary prayers (nawāfil) according to the Naqshbandi path?
b: After attaining spiritual stability and minor annihilation, when his heart becomes firmly established in servitude to Allah and detached from other than Him, he becomes suited to increase voluntary prayers as a means of drawing closer to Allah.

f: Why do the Naqshbandi shaykhs emphasize voluntary prayers after spiritual realization?
b: Because voluntary prayers are among the greatest means of attaining closeness to Allah and reaching higher spiritual ranks.

f: What role do voluntary prayers play in the spiritual path?
b: Voluntary prayers lead to the attainment of true spiritual states (aḥwāl), true spiritual states lead to correct unveiling (kashf), and correct unveiling leads to knowledge of Allah (maʿrifah).

f: What is the progression described between worship and spiritual realization?
b: Voluntary worship → sincere spiritual states → correct unveiling → knowledge of Allah, which is described as the manifest light resulting from the manifestation of the Divine Essence.

f: What hadith qudsi is used as evidence for the importance of voluntary worship?
b: Allah says: "My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him."

f: What happens when Allah loves His servant according to the hadith qudsi?
b: Allah becomes the servant's hearing by which he hears, his sight by which he sees, his hand by which he strikes, and his foot by which he walks. If he asks Allah, Allah gives him; and if he seeks refuge with Him, Allah protects him.

f: Does focusing on voluntary prayers after spiritual realization mean that the seeker neglected voluntary prayers before that point?
b: No. It means that after attaining spiritual realization and firmness, he becomes more devoted to all forms of worship because his heart has become fully established in servitude to Allah.

f: Why do the awliyāʾ increase in voluntary worship after spiritual realization?
b: Because Allah grants them the ability to turn toward Him with complete sincerity, after their hearts have been emptied of attachment to other than Him.

f: What is the relationship between the servant's closeness to Allah and Allah's closeness to the servant?
b: When the servant approaches Allah through obedience, Allah responds with greater closeness, mercy, and favor.

f: What hadith describes Allah drawing closer to His servant when the servant approaches Him?
b: Allah says: "If My servant draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length; if he draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running."

f: What is the highest purpose of voluntary acts of worship according to the hadith qudsi?
b: Their highest purpose is attaining Allah's love.

f: What is the relationship between obligatory and voluntary worship in attaining Allah's love?
b: Obligatory worship is the foundation of closeness to Allah, and voluntary worship completes and increases that closeness until Allah loves the servant.

f: What does the hadith "My servant continues drawing near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him" teach about spiritual perfection?
b: It teaches that spiritual perfection comes through continuous obedience, beginning with obligations and being perfected through voluntary worship until divine love is attained.

f: What are the daily spiritual practices (awrād) of the Naqshbandi path divided into?
b: They are divided into two categories: practices specific to the night and practices specific to the day.

f: What are the night practices (awrād al-layl) in the Naqshbandi path?
b: The night practices include Ṣalāt al-Awwābīn between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ (six to twelve rakʿahs) and Ṣalāt al-Tahajjud after sleep in the last third of the night (twelve rakʿahs).

f: What are the daytime practices (awrād al-nahār) in the Naqshbandi path?
b: The daytime practices include Ṣalāt al-Ishrāq (two to four rakʿahs after the sun rises about the height of a spear) and Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā (four to eight rakʿahs after the first quarter of the day).

f: Which voluntary prayers are considered the established awrād of the Naqshbandi path?
b: Ṣalāt al-Awwābīn, Ṣalāt al-Tahajjud, Ṣalāt al-Ishrāq, and Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā are considered the established voluntary prayers of the Naqshbandi path.

f: What should the seeker who has reached minor sainthood (al-wilāyah al-ṣughrā) do with these voluntary prayers?
b: He should make these voluntary prayers his regular spiritual practices (awrād) and remain consistent with them.

f: If the seeker wants to increase his voluntary prayers beyond the established Naqshbandi awrād, how should he do so?
b: He may pray additional voluntary prayers with the intention of performing nawāfil.

f: What happens when minor sainthood reaches its completion and the seeker attains major sainthood (al-wilāyah al-kubrā)?
b: The seeker becomes qualified to engage extensively in recitation of the Qur'an and other forms of remembrance because he has reached the rank associated with the sainthood of the prophets.

f: Why is recitation of the Qur'an especially emphasized after reaching major sainthood?
b: Because at this level the seeker can draw closer to Allah through every form of remembrance, and the Qur'an is the greatest form of dhikr for attaining closeness to Allah.

f: How does a person at the rank of major sainthood experience Qur'an recitation?
b: He witnesses different forms of divine manifestations (tajalliyāt) while reciting different verses with different meanings.

f: Why is recitation of the Qur'an considered among the greatest ways of drawing near to Allah?
b: Because the Qur'an is the speech of the Lord of the worlds, miraculous and eternal, and reciting it exposes the servant to Allah's mercy and blessings.

f: What Quranic command is mentioned regarding reciting the Qur'an?
b: Allah commands: "And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation" (Qur'an 73:4).

f: How does Allah describe those who regularly recite His Book?
b: Allah praises those who recite His Book, establish prayer, and spend from what He has provided, promising them a trade that will never perish and an increase from His bounty (Qur'an 35:29-30).

f: How did the Prophet ﷺ compare the believer who recites the Qur'an?
b: He compared the believer who recites the Qur'an to a citron (utrūjah): its smell is pleasant and its taste is pleasant.

f: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the believer who does not recite the Qur'an?
b: He compared such a believer to a date: it has no fragrance but its taste is sweet.

f: How did the Prophet ﷺ compare hypocrites in relation to Qur'an recitation?
b: He compared the hypocrite who recites the Qur'an to a fragrant flower with a bitter taste, and the hypocrite who does not recite it to a bitter fruit with no fragrance.

f: What are the two things in which envy is permitted according to the hadith?
b: Envy is permitted regarding a person whom Allah has given the Qur'an and who recites it throughout the night and day, and a person whom Allah has given wealth and who spends it throughout the night and day.

f: What does the hadith "Allah raises people through this Book and lowers others through it" mean?
b: It means that those who honor, learn, and act upon the Qur'an are elevated by Allah, while those who neglect or oppose it are lowered.

f: What role will the Qur'an play on the Day of Judgment?
b: The Qur'an will come as an intercessor for those who were devoted to it.

f: Who did the Prophet ﷺ describe as the best among people?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it."

f: What blessings descend upon gatherings where people recite and study the Qur'an?
b: Tranquility descends upon them, mercy covers them, angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those near Him.

f: What reward is mentioned for reciting each letter of the Qur'an?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever recites one letter from the Book of Allah receives one good deed, and each good deed is multiplied tenfold. He clarified that "Alif-Lām-Mīm" is not one letter, but rather Alif is a letter, Lām is a letter, and Mīm is a letter.

f: Who are described as the special people of Allah (Ahl Allāh wa khāṣṣatuh)?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said that the people of the Qur'an are the special people of Allah and His chosen ones.

f: What does the title "people of the Qur'an" indicate?
b: It indicates those who are devoted to the Qur'an through recitation, learning, memorization, and acting upon its guidance.

f: What role will the Qur'an have for its companions on the Day of Judgment?
b: The Qur'an will come as an intercessor for those who were devoted to it.

f: What will be said to the companion of the Qur'an on the Day of Judgment?
b: It will be said: "Recite and ascend, and recite with measured recitation as you used to recite in the world, for your rank will be at the last verse you recite."

f: What is the reward of the person skilled in reciting the Qur'an?
b: The person proficient in the Qur'an will be with the noble and obedient angels.

f: What is the reward of the person who recites the Qur'an with difficulty?
b: The person who recites the Qur'an while struggling and stumbling receives a double reward.

f: How is Qur'an recitation organized as a regular practice (wird) in the Naqshbandi path?
b: Qur'an recitation is assigned at specific times of the day and night as part of the regular spiritual practices of the path.

f: Which surah is recited after the Fajr prayer as part of the Naqshbandi Qur'an wird?
b: Sūrat Yā-Sīn is recited after the Fajr prayer.

f: Which surah is recited after the Ẓuhr prayer as part of the Naqshbandi Qur'an wird?
b: Sūrat al-Mulk is recited after the Ẓuhr prayer.

f: Which surah is recited after the ʿAṣr prayer as part of the Naqshbandi Qur'an wird?
b: Sūrat al-Nabaʾ is recited after the ʿAṣr prayer.

f: Which surah is recited after Ṣalāt al-Awwābīn as part of the Naqshbandi Qur'an wird?
b: Sūrat al-Sajdah is recited after Ṣalāt al-Awwābīn.

f: Which surah is recited after the ʿIshāʾ prayer as part of the Naqshbandi Qur'an wird?
b: Sūrat al-Mulk is recited after the ʿIshāʾ prayer.

f: Which Qur'anic passages are recited before sleeping in the Naqshbandi practice?
b: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, the two protective surahs (al-Muʿawwidhatayn), the ending verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and the ending of Sūrat al-Ḥashr are recited before sleep.

f: What additional Qur'an-related practice exists in the Naqshbandi path besides individual recitation?
b: The Naqshbandi path includes another practice called Khatm al-Khwājagān (the Completion/Seal of the Masters), which is a regular collective gathering of remembrance and recitation.

f: What does the term "Khwājagān" mean?
b: Khwājagān is a Persian term meaning "the shaykhs" or "masters." Its singular form is Khwāja (also pronounced Khāja).

f: Why is it called "Khatm al-Khwājagān" (the Seal of the Masters)?
b: It is called this because the Naqshbandi masters used to conclude their gatherings with this practice.

f: What is Khatm al-Khwājagān in the Naqshbandi tradition?
b: It is a collective circle of remembrance (dhikr) that disciples regularly perform, following the example of the gatherings of remembrance held by the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.

f: Who is permitted to perform Khatm al-Khwājagān according to the Naqshbandi tradition?
b: It is specifically for the disciples of the Naqshbandi path and those who have received permission (ijāzah) to perform it.

f: What is the reward of reciting the Qur'an while finding it difficult?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said that the one who recites the Qur'an while it is difficult for him receives two rewards.

f: What hadith is mentioned regarding gatherings of remembrance?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When you pass by the gardens of Paradise, graze there." They asked: "What are the gardens of Paradise?" He replied: "The circles of remembrance."

f: What are the virtues of gatherings of dhikr mentioned in the hadith?
b: When people gather to remember Allah, angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and Allah mentions them among those with Him.

f: What does the hadith about angels searching for gatherings of remembrance teach?
b: It teaches that angels seek gatherings where Allah is remembered, surround those attending them, and Allah forgives the people present in those gatherings.

f: What does the statement "They are the people sitting together; their companion will not be deprived" mean?
b: It means that even a person who attends a gathering of remembrance without the same intention or level of devotion as the others may still receive Allah's mercy because of the righteous people accompanying him.

f: What precedent from the Companions is used as evidence for collective dhikr gatherings?
b: The practice of the Companions, such as Salmān al-Fārisī and others, gathering for remembrance of Allah with the approval of the Prophet ﷺ, is cited as evidence.

f: Why does the Naqshbandi tradition emphasize Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Because it combines Qur'an recitation and remembrance of Allah in a structured gathering, following the practice of righteous predecessors and seeking the blessings associated with collective dhikr.

f: How is Khatm al-Khwājagān begun in the Naqshbandi tradition?
b: Before beginning the khatm, the participants recite a specific supplication after saying the basmalah.

f: What supplication is recited before Khatm al-Khwājagān begins?
b: The supplication is: "O Allah, Opener of doors, Turner of hearts and eyes, Guide of those who are confused, Helper of those who seek help. I rely upon You, O Lord of the worlds. I entrust my affair to Allah; indeed Allah sees His servants. There is no power nor strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great."

f: How many times is Sūrat al-Fātiḥah recited at the beginning of Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah is recited seven times.

f: How many times are blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ recited during Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Ṣalawāt upon the Prophet ﷺ are recited one hundred times at the beginning and another one hundred times at the end.

f: How many times is Sūrat al-Sharḥ ("Alam Nashraḥ Laka") recited in Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Sūrat al-Sharḥ is recited seventy-nine times.

f: How many times is Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ recited in Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ is recited one thousand and one times.

f: How is Khatm al-Khwājagān concluded?
b: After reciting Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ one thousand and one times, Sūrat al-Fātiḥah is recited seven times, followed by one hundred ṣalawāt upon the Prophet ﷺ.

f: What condition is mentioned regarding the recitations in Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: The recitations should be performed together in one gathering with a group engaged in the remembrance of Allah.

f: What type of gathering is Khatm al-Khwājagān considered to be?
b: It is considered a gathering of dhikr where people collectively remember Allah through Qur'an recitation, prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ, and supplication.

f: What evidence is mentioned for gatherings of remembrance involving groups of people?
b: A narration is mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ passed by companions who were gathered remembering Allah. He approached them and said that he saw mercy descending upon them and wished to share in it.

f: How do Naqshbandi scholars respond to those who consider Khatm al-Khwājagān a blameworthy innovation?
b: They argue that not every newly organized practice is condemned, especially if it is done seeking Allah's pleasure and is based upon permissible acts of worship such as Qur'an recitation and dhikr.

f: What Quranic verse is used regarding practices introduced by previous communities for seeking Allah's pleasure?
b: Allah says regarding the followers of Jesus ﷺ: "And monasticism which they invented — We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of Allah, but they did not observe it as it should have been observed..." (Qur'an 57:27).

f: What lesson is derived from Qur'an 57:27 regarding religious practices?
b: The criticism was not that they created a practice seeking Allah's pleasure, but that they failed to fulfill it properly. The intention and sincerity behind the practice are important.

f: What intention is emphasized during Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: The participants maintain the intention: "My Lord, You are my مَقْصِدٌ (ultimate aim), and Your pleasure is my goal."

f: What condition is mentioned regarding the recitation of the surahs in Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Each surah should be recited with the basmalah every time it is read, and seeking refuge (istiʿādhah) should be said at the beginning of the recitation.

f: How are the surahs distributed when Khatm al-Khwājagān is performed as a group?
b: The recitations are divided among the members of the gathering according to the number of participants.

f: What is done with the reward (thawāb) after completing Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: The reward is gifted to the souls of the Khwājagān (the Naqshbandi masters) and other righteous souls.

f: What is done after gifting the reward to the righteous souls?
b: The participants seek their need from Allah through the blessing (barakah) associated with them.

f: What is traditionally done after completing Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Whatever sweets are available may be distributed after completion.

f: What are the etiquettes (ādāb) of Khatm al-Khwājagān at the beginning?
b: The participants close their eyes and recite istighfār five, fifteen, or twenty-five times.

f: What is done after the initial istighfār in Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: The participant performs the "noble rābiṭah" (spiritual connection) for a moment and then turns attention toward the heart for heart-presence (wuqūf qalbī).

f: What is wuqūf qalbī during Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: It is maintaining awareness and attention of the heart toward Allah throughout the entire khatm from beginning to end.

f: Why is heart-presence (wuqūf qalbī) considered necessary during Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Because the recitation is not intended to be merely verbal; the heart should remain attentive to Allah, the One whose speech is being recited.

f: What are the three levels of Qur'an recitation mentioned regarding spiritual awareness?
b: The common people recite the words, the special people recite while contemplating the meanings, and the most select people turn their hearts toward the Speaker Himself, Allah, while awaiting divine spiritual gifts.

f: How does the recitation of the most spiritually advanced people differ from ordinary recitation?
b: They do not merely focus on pronunciation or meanings; their hearts become directed toward Allah Himself, with awareness of His Divine Essence and expectation of spiritual openings.

f: What does "awaiting the Divine effusion (fayḍ ilāhī)" mean in this context?
b: It means remaining spiritually receptive and hoping for Allah to grant illumination, knowledge, and blessings to the heart during the recitation.

f: What additional etiquette is mentioned during Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Seeking spiritual attention and blessing (tawajjuh and fayḍ) from the spiritual presence of the shaykhs.

f: Who is attributed with establishing the original Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: The original khatm is attributed to Shaykh ʿAbd al-Khāliq al-Ghujdawānī.

f: Why are there different forms of Khatm al-Khwājagān among Naqshbandi shaykhs?
b: Each shaykh in different times adapted the practice according to the capacity of disciples and what would benefit them spiritually.

f: Which Naqshbandi masters are mentioned as having their own versions of Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: Versions are attributed to masters such as Shāh Naqshband, ʿUbayd Allāh al-Aḥrār, Muḥammad al-Bāqī, Imām al-Sirhindī, ʿAbd Allāh al-Dihlawī, and Khālid al-Baghdādī.

f: What did some earlier Naqshbandi shaykhs distribute to participants after gatherings of Khatm al-Khwājagān?
b: They distributed honey to the people of the gathering when they were able to do so.

f: What is the purpose of the additional Qur'an recitations (awrad) in the Naqshbandi path?
b: They are prescribed as regular devotional practices (awrad) to help the seeker maintain remembrance of Allah, strengthen spiritual discipline, and increase closeness to Allah through Qur'an recitation.

f: Are the Qur'an recitations prescribed in the Naqshbandi path the only Qur'an recitations a seeker may perform?
b: No. These are specific awrad of the Naqshbandi path, but a seeker may recite any other portions of the Qur'an in addition to them.

f: Is it permissible for a seeker to read Qur'an beyond the awrad assigned by his shaykh?
b: Yes. After completing the prescribed awrad, the seeker may read whatever he wishes from the Qur'an and other forms of remembrance of Allah.

f: What other acts of worship may a seeker add after completing his prescribed awrad?
b: He may engage in additional Qur'an recitation, supplications, formulas of praise upon the Prophet ﷺ, voluntary prayers, and other acts that bring one closer to Allah.

f: Which is considered better: reciting the prescribed awrad outside prayer or reciting Qur'an during prayer?
b: Qur'an recitation within prayer is considered superior because prayer combines Qur'an recitation with standing before Allah in worship.

f: What concern does the author address regarding limiting oneself to the prescribed awrad?
b: He clarifies that following the awrad of the shaykh does not prevent the seeker from engaging in other forms of worship and remembrance.

f: What is the principle behind the Naqshbandi awrad and additional acts of worship?
b: The purpose is not restriction but organization: the seeker maintains the discipline of the prescribed awrad while increasing his devotion through other permissible acts of worship.

f: What is the role of companionship (ṣuḥbah) with the shaykhs in the spiritual paths?
b: Companionship with the shaykhs is considered an independent means of reaching spiritual perfection because the seeker benefits from the guidance, example, and spiritual state of the perfected teacher.

f: Why is the chapter on companionship with shaykhs considered important in the path of spiritual training?
b: Because proper manners (adab) form the foundation of the relationship between the shaykh and the seeker, between seekers themselves, and between the seeker and creation. These manners help overcome inner obstacles during spiritual development.

f: What does the concept of adab in the relationship between shaykh and murid represent?
b: It represents a refined relationship based on respect, following a worthy example, and proper conduct, following the example of the Companions in their relationship with the Prophet ﷺ.

f: Is respecting the shaykh considered worship or excessive glorification of the shaykh?
b: No. It is not considered worship or sanctification of the shaykh, but rather respect for a teacher, guide, and role model whose example helps in moral and spiritual education.

f: What is the linguistic meaning of ṣuḥbah (companionship)?
b: Linguistically, ṣuḥbah means accompanying, associating with, being close to, and remaining with someone. It carries the meaning of companionship, familiarity, and attachment.

f: How is ṣuḥbah defined in spiritual terminology?
b: It refers to the seeker remaining with his shaykh for the purpose of spiritual training, purification, learning, and progressing in spiritual states. It can also refer to the lessons, advice, and guidance given by the shaykh.

f: What Qur'anic example illustrates the meaning of following a teacher for guidance?
b: The story of Musa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ and al-Khaḍir عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, when Musa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ said: “May I follow you so that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound guidance?” (Qur'an 18:66).

f: Why is companionship with a perfected shaykh considered central in spiritual paths?
b: Because the path to spiritual realization is based upon companionship with perfected shaykhs and the advice of guides who have already reached the destination.

f: What can a perfected shaykh provide for a sincere seeker through companionship?
b: A perfected shaykh can help the sincere seeker reach spiritual perfection, unveil the lights of divine majesty and beauty, and reveal the realities of spiritual stations without requiring the seeker to rely solely on prolonged exercises, abundant practices, or constant spiritual struggle.

f: According to the author, what is the importance of the perfected shaykh compared to spiritual practices alone?
b: The perfected shaykh's companionship can accelerate the seeker's progress because the shaykh transmits guidance, spiritual states, and understanding that cannot always be gained through practices alone.

f: What were those who entered the companionship of the Prophet ﷺ called?
b: Those who entered the companionship of the Prophet ﷺ were known as the Ṣaḥābah (Companions).

f: What names were given to those who entered the companionship of spiritual teachers after the Companions?
b: Their names varied according to time and circumstance, including companions, students, disciples, and murīds (spiritual seekers).

f: Does the author claim that one spiritual path is superior to all others?
b: No. The author explains that the shaykh benefits from all the recognized spiritual paths and does not blindly favor his own path without recognizing the virtues of others.

f: Why do the various spiritual paths share common principles despite differences in methods?
b: Because all authentic paths aim at the same goal: purifying the heart, cleansing the soul, and directing the servant toward Allah. Their foundations are based on the Qur'an and Sunnah, while their methods may differ.

f: What does the statement “the paths to Allah are as numerous as the number of seekers who desire Him” mean?
b: It means that there are many possible ways and approaches through which people may reach closeness to Allah, according to their circumstances, abilities, and spiritual dispositions.

f: What is the common foundation shared by the spiritual paths?
b: The common foundation is purification of the heart, obedience to Allah, following the Prophet ﷺ, and spiritual refinement according to the Qur'an and Sunnah.

f: What is meant by a “perfect shaykh” (shaykh kāmil)?
b: A perfect shaykh is one qualified to guide seekers through spiritual training, being a true inheritor of the Prophet ﷺ in knowledge, practice, character, and purification.

f: What qualifications does a shaykh kāmil possess according to the author?
b: He has reached complete sainthood (wilāyah), has authorization to train and guide seekers, and possesses a genuine connected spiritual chain of authorization reaching back to the Prophet ﷺ.

f: Who cannot be considered a perfect shaykh?
b: A person who merely claims spiritual status, lacks knowledge, has no authentic connection of authorization, or is spiritually heedless cannot be considered a perfect shaykh.

f: Can someone be a saint (walī) without being qualified to train others?
b: Yes. A person may possess sainthood, goodness, blessings, and remembrance of Allah, but still lack the qualifications necessary for educating disciples, guiding seekers, and purifying hearts.

f: What is the difference between a saintly person and a spiritual guide qualified to train disciples?
b: A saintly person may have closeness to Allah and spiritual blessings, while a qualified guide must additionally possess knowledge, authorization, and the ability to direct others on the path of purification.

f: Why does the seeker need a perfected shaykh in the path of spiritual realization?
b: Because the shaykh has greater knowledge of the means of reaching Allah and can guide the seeker through the stages of spiritual development based on experience and insight.

f: Are all people required to reach Allah through the same method of spiritual struggle and discipline?
b: No. Some servants reach Allah through divine selection and attraction (jadhb and ijtibā’), while others progress through guidance, spiritual struggle, and disciplined practices. Both are paths of goodness.

f: What does it mean that some people reach Allah through divine attraction (ijtabā’)?
b: It means that Allah may open a person’s heart and bring him close through His grace and choosing, without requiring extensive outward struggle, due to sincerity and truthful turning toward Him.

f: What Qur'anic principle supports the idea that Allah may choose whom He wills and guide those who turn to Him?
b: The verse: “Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back to Him” (Qur'an 42:13).

f: What does the author say about spiritual exercises (riyāḍāt) without the companionship of perfected shaykhs?
b: He says that spiritual exercises without the companionship and training of perfected shaykhs only produce confusion and spiritual whisperings rather than true realization.

f: Why does the author emphasize the companionship of a perfected shaykh over personal spiritual exercises?
b: Because the benefit gained through the companionship of a perfected shaykh in a single moment may not be achieved through reading thousands of books or performing spiritual exercises for thousands of years.

f: What is the role of the perfected shaykh in relation to the seeker (murīd)?
b: The perfected shaykh spiritually guides and influences the seeker through companionship, helping him progress toward the station of spiritual witnessing (mushāhadah).

f: According to the author, can the station of mushāhadah be reached without companionship of a perfected shaykh?
b: The author states that this station cannot be reached in the proper manner without the companionship of a perfected shaykh.

f: What statement of Khwāja Bahā’ al-Dīn Naqshband summarizes the importance of companionship?
