f: Who received the transmission after Muhammad Baqi?
b: Ahmad Sirhindi قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission after Muhammad Baqi.

f: How is Ahmad Sirhindi described?
b: He is described as the imam who manifested wonders and was a source of secrets and meanings, known as Imam Rabbani and the Reviver of the Second Millennium (Mujaddid Alf Thani).

f: Why is Ahmad Sirhindi given the title “Mujaddid Alf Thani”?
b: Because he is regarded in the Naqshbandi-Mujaddidi tradition as a renewer of the religious and spiritual understanding of Islam in the second Islamic millennium.

f: Who received the transmission after Ahmad Sirhindi?
b: His son Muhammad Maʿsum قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Muhammad Maʿsum described?
b: He is described as the noble son, keeper of his father’s hidden spiritual secret, and a master among masters.

f: Who received the transmission after Muhammad Maʿsum?
b: His son Sheikh Sayf al-Din قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Sheikh Sayf al-Din described?
b: He is described as the one immersed in the ocean of the reality of certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn), and a sultan among the awliyāʾ.

f: Who received the transmission after Sheikh Sayf al-Din?
b: Sayyid Nur Muhammad al-Badauni قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Sayyid Nur Muhammad al-Badauni described?
b: He is described as the imam honored by Divine self-manifestation and Divine attributes, and the master of masters.

f: Who received the transmission after Sayyid Nur Muhammad al-Badauni?
b: Shams al-Din Habib Allah al-Marjani al-Mazhar قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Shams al-Din Habib Allah al-Marjani described?
b: He is described as the purified, chosen, perfected imam who manifested spiritual light.

f: Who received the transmission after Shams al-Din Habib Allah al-Marjani?
b: Abdullah al-Dahlawi قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Abdullah al-Dahlawi described?
b: He is described as the pole of the saints and proof of the pious, combining outward and inward perfection.

f: Who received the transmission after Abdullah al-Dahlawi?
b: Khalid al-Baghdadi قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Khalid al-Baghdadi described?
b: He is described as the pole of spiritual guidance (qutb al-irshad), the traveler in Allah, the one who bows and prostrates, possessing two wings.

f: Who received the transmission after Khalid al-Baghdadi?
b: Sheikh Ismail al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قُدِّسَ سِرُّهُ received the transmission.

f: Who was Ismail al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ according to the note?
b: He was the one who called people to Allah and spread the Naqshbandi path in Dagestan and the Caucasus regions.

f: Who received the transmission after Ismail al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ?
b: Sheikh Khas Muhammad al-Shirwani قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Khas Muhammad al-Shirwani described?
b: He is described as the imam who connects seekers to their spiritual aspirations and goals.

f: Who received the transmission after Khas Muhammad al-Shirwani?
b: Sheikh Muhammad al-Yaraghi قُدِّسَ سِرُّه received the transmission.

f: How is Muhammad al-Yaraghi described?
b: He is described as the imam who gathered virtues, honors, and excellences.

f: Who is the final person mentioned as receiving the transmission in this chain?
b: Jamal al-Din, the humble and needy servant, is mentioned as the final recipient of the transmission.

f: How does Jamal al-Din describe himself?
b: He describes himself as weak, poor, possessing deficiency and shortcomings, asking Allah to illuminate him with the light of spiritual witnessing.

f: What is the meaning of the concluding poetic statement: “Those are my fathers; bring me their equals…”?
b: It expresses pride in the spiritual lineage of the Naqshbandi masters and challenges anyone to present equals to them in knowledge, spiritual training, asceticism, and humility.

f: What qualities does the author praise in the Naqshbandi masters at the end of the chain?
b: He praises their knowledge, ability to spiritually train others (sulūk), asceticism, humility, poverty before Allah, and spiritual excellence.

f: Why is there a difference in mentioning Ismaʿil al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ and Ismaʿil al-Shirwani عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ in the Naqshbandi chain after Mawlana Khalid?
b: The author explains that Mawlana Khalid al-Baghdadi sent Ismaʿil al-Shirwani عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ to spread the path in those lands and granted him complete authorization (khilāfah). However, shortly before his death, Ismaʿil al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ authorized Sheikh Khas Muhammad Afandi, creating another valid connection in the chain.

f: Who was Ismaʿil al-Shirwani عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ in relation to Mawlana Khalid al-Baghdadi?
b: He was one of Mawlana Khalid’s authorized successors who was sent to spread the Naqshbandi path in Dagestan and the Caucasus and was granted complete spiritual authorization.

f: Who was Ismaʿil al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ in relation to Mawlana Khalid al-Baghdadi?
b: He was the guardian and representative over all of Mawlana Khalid’s successors and later authorized Sheikh Khas Muhammad Afandi shortly before his death.

f: Why may either Ismaʿil al-Shirwani عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ or Ismaʿil al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ be mentioned in the spiritual chain?
b: Because both received authorization connected to Mawlana Khalid’s spiritual transmission, and both provide a valid route of transmission.

f: Which name was included in later versions of the chain according to the author?
b: Later choices often mentioned Ismaʿil al-Kurdamiri عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ alone rather than Ismaʿil al-Shirwani عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ.

f: Through whom does the author say this blessed chain reaches them?
b: The author says the chain reaches them through Mawlana Sheikh Muhammad Nazim al-Haqqani and Mawlana Sheikh Husayn Ali al-Rabbani رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

f: Through whom did Muhammad Nazim al-Haqqani and Husayn Ali al-Rabbani رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ receive the chain?
b: They received it through Sheikh Abdullah al-Fa’iz al-Daghestani.

f: Through whom did Sheikh Abdullah al-Fa’iz al-Daghestani receive the chain?
b: He received it through Sheikh Sharaf al-Din al-Daghestani.

f: Through whom did Sheikh Sharaf al-Din al-Daghestani receive the chain?
b: He received it through Sheikh Abu Muhammad al-Madani.

f: Through whom did Sheikh Abu Muhammad al-Madani receive the chain?
b: He received it through Sheikh Abu Ahmad al-Thaghuri.

f: Through whom did Sheikh Abu Ahmad al-Thaghuri receive the chain?
b: He received it through Sheikh Jamal al-Din al-Ghumuki قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ أَسْرَارَهُمْ.

f: What qualities does the author attribute to the Naqshbandi masters in the closing advice?
b: He describes them as people who adhered firmly to the Muhammadan Sharia, sought only Allah’s pleasure, purified themselves from human desires, purified their actions from showing off, ate only lawful things, and received divine gifts and openings.

f: How does the author describe the spiritual state of the Naqshbandi masters?
b: He says they purified themselves from base desires until they became like spiritual beings, were granted divine openings, and had their hearts and chests opened to hidden knowledge and spiritual joy.

f: What should someone who wishes to follow this path do?
b: They should adhere to the practices and remembrances of the masters, follow their spiritual states and actions, and strive to imitate their way.

f: Does the author say that merely having a connection to the spiritual lineage is sufficient?
b: No. He warns the seeker not to rely only on noble lineage or association, because true rank comes through righteous deeds and sincere effort.

f: What warning does the author give about relying on spiritual ancestry?
b: He warns that relying on lineage alone can lead to failure and hardship, because spiritual elevation comes through action, not merely through connection to predecessors.

f: What does the statement “Whoever performs righteous deeds rises to the highest degrees” mean?
b: It means that spiritual rank is attained through obedience, sincerity, and good actions rather than through claims of status or ancestry.

f: What does the poem at the end emphasize about reaching spiritual perfection?
b: The poem emphasizes that the people of spiritual excellence reached high ranks through effort, sincerity, and good deeds; whoever desires this path must sacrifice comfort and dedicate themselves fully.

f: What does the phrase “the path of the beloved is not easy” mean?
b: It means that reaching closeness to Allah requires struggle, patience, purification of the soul, and sincere devotion.

f: What does the poet mean by “make your provision sincere deeds”?
b: The seeker’s true provision on the spiritual journey is sincerity and righteous action, not worldly possessions or claims of status.
